title: Afghanistan
text: Afghanistan is a landlocked country in South-Central Asia, with Kabul as its capital. Its official languages are Pashto and Dari. The rugged Hindu Kush mountain range dominates much of its terrain, and it shares borders with Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and China.

title: Albania
text: Albania is a country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Tirana as its capital. Albanian is the official language. It lies along the Adriatic and Ionian Seas, facing Italy across the Strait of Otranto, and its terrain is largely mountainous.

title: Algeria
text: Algeria is a large country in North Africa, with Algiers as its capital on the Mediterranean coast. Arabic and Berber are official languages. Much of its vast interior lies within the Sahara Desert, and it is the largest country by area on the African continent.

title: Andorra
text: Andorra is a small landlocked microstate in the eastern Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain, with Andorra la Vella as its capital. Catalan is the official language. It is known for skiing, mountain scenery, and its status as a co-principality.

title: Angola
text: Angola is a country in Southern Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Luanda as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It is rich in oil and diamonds, and the Kwanza River flows through its territory.

title: Antigua and Barbuda
text: Antigua and Barbuda is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea, part of the Lesser Antilles, with Saint John's as its capital. English is the official language. It is known for its many beaches and coral reefs.

title: Argentina
text: Argentina is a large country in southern South America, with Buenos Aires as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It stretches from the subtropical north to the Patagonian south, and it shares the Iguazu Falls and the Andes mountains, including Aconcagua, the highest peak in the Americas.

title: Armenia
text: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus region, with Yerevan as its capital. Armenian is the official language. It is a mountainous nation and was one of the first states to adopt Christianity as a state religion. Mount Ararat is a national symbol.

title: Australia
text: Australia is a country and continent in the Southern Hemisphere, with Canberra as its capital. English is the primary language. Surrounded by the Indian and Pacific Oceans, it is known for the Great Barrier Reef, Uluru, and a vast arid interior called the Outback.

title: Austria
text: Austria is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with Vienna as its capital. German is the official language. The Alps cover much of the country, and it is famous for classical music, historic architecture, and the Danube River.

title: Azerbaijan
text: Azerbaijan is a country in the South Caucasus on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, with Baku as its capital. Azerbaijani is the official language. It is known for its oil reserves and a landscape ranging from mountains to lowlands.

title: Bahamas
text: The Bahamas is an archipelago nation in the Atlantic Ocean, northeast of Cuba, with Nassau as its capital. English is the official language. It comprises hundreds of islands and cays and is known for clear waters and tourism.

title: Bahrain
text: Bahrain is a small island country in the Persian Gulf off the coast of Saudi Arabia, with Manama as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It is connected to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway and has a long history of pearl diving.

title: Bangladesh
text: Bangladesh is a densely populated country in South Asia, with Dhaka as its capital. Bengali is the official language. It lies largely on the fertile Ganges-Brahmaputra delta and borders the Bay of Bengal, and it is home to part of the Sundarbans mangrove forest.

title: Barbados
text: Barbados is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, part of the Lesser Antilles, with Bridgetown as its capital. English is the official language. It is known for its beaches, coral reefs, and sugar-cane heritage.

title: Belarus
text: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, with Minsk as its capital. Belarusian and Russian are official languages. It has extensive forests and marshes and shares the ancient Bialowieza Forest with Poland.

title: Belgium
text: Belgium is a country in Western Europe, with Brussels as its capital, which also hosts the headquarters of the European Union. Dutch, French, and German are official languages. It is known for medieval towns, chocolate, and the North Sea coast.

title: Belize
text: Belize is a country on the northeastern coast of Central America, with Belmopan as its capital. English is the official language. It borders the Caribbean Sea and is known for the Belize Barrier Reef and dense rainforest.

title: Benin
text: Benin is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Porto-Novo as its official capital and Cotonou as its seat of government. French is the official language. It is regarded as the birthplace of the Vodun religion.

title: Bhutan
text: Bhutan is a landlocked kingdom in the eastern Himalayas, with Thimphu as its capital. Dzongkha is the official language. Known for its measure of Gross National Happiness, it is a Buddhist nation with dramatic mountain monasteries such as Paro Taktsang.

title: Bolivia
text: Bolivia is a landlocked country in central South America, with Sucre as its constitutional capital and La Paz as its seat of government. Spanish and several Indigenous languages are official. It contains the Altiplano highlands and the vast Salar de Uyuni salt flat.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Sarajevo as its capital. Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian are official languages. It is mostly mountainous, with a short coastline on the Adriatic Sea.

title: Botswana
text: Botswana is a landlocked country in Southern Africa, with Gaborone as its capital. English and Setswana are widely used. Much of its territory lies within the Kalahari Desert, and it contains the wildlife-rich Okavango Delta.

title: Brazil
text: Brazil is the largest country in South America, with Brasilia as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It contains most of the Amazon rainforest and river basin, borders the Atlantic Ocean, and is known for Rio de Janeiro and the Iguazu Falls.

title: Brunei
text: Brunei is a small country on the island of Borneo in Southeast Asia, with Bandar Seri Begawan as its capital. Malay is the official language. It borders the South China Sea and is known for its oil wealth and tropical rainforest.

title: Bulgaria
text: Bulgaria is a country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Sofia as its capital. Bulgarian is the official language, written in the Cyrillic alphabet. It borders the Black Sea and features the Balkan and Rila mountain ranges.

title: Burkina Faso
text: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa, with Ouagadougou as its capital. French is the official language. It lies within the Sahel region between the Sahara and the wetter south, with a largely flat savanna landscape.

title: Burundi
text: Burundi is a small landlocked country in East Africa's Great Lakes region, with Gitega as its political capital and Bujumbura as its largest city. Kirundi and French are official languages. It lies near Lake Tanganyika.

title: Cambodia
text: Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia, with Phnom Penh as its capital. Khmer is the official language. It borders the Gulf of Thailand and is famous for the temple complex of Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.

title: Cameroon
text: Cameroon is a country in Central Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Yaounde as its capital. French and English are official languages. Its varied terrain includes coastline, mountains, rainforest, and savanna, and Mount Cameroon is an active volcano.

title: Canada
text: Canada is a vast country in North America, with Ottawa as its capital. English and French are official languages. Bordered by three oceans, it is known for the Rocky Mountains, Niagara Falls, extensive boreal forests, and the Great Lakes shared with the United States.

title: Cape Verde
text: Cape Verde, officially Cabo Verde, is an island nation in the Atlantic Ocean off West Africa, with Praia as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It is a volcanic archipelago known for its music and Creole culture.

title: Central African Republic
text: The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in Central Africa, with Bangui as its capital. French and Sango are official languages. It contains savanna and rainforest and is drained by the Ubangi River.

title: Chad
text: Chad is a landlocked country in North-Central Africa, with N'Djamena as its capital. French and Arabic are official languages. It contains part of the Sahara Desert in the north and Lake Chad, a large but shrinking lake, in the west.

title: Chile
text: Chile is a long, narrow country along the western coast of South America, with Santiago as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It stretches from the arid Atacama Desert to Patagonia and is bounded by the Andes and the Pacific Ocean.

title: China
text: China is a large country in East Asia, with Beijing as its capital. Standard Mandarin Chinese is the official language. It borders the Pacific Ocean and is known for the Great Wall, the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers, and diverse landscapes from deserts to mountains.

title: Colombia
text: Colombia is a country in northwestern South America, with Bogota as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean, and the Andes mountains run through its western regions.

title: Comoros
text: The Comoros is an island nation in the Indian Ocean off the coast of East Africa, with Moroni as its capital. Comorian, Arabic, and French are official languages. It is a volcanic archipelago between Madagascar and mainland Africa.

title: Republic of the Congo
text: The Republic of the Congo is a country in Central Africa, with Brazzaville as its capital, located on the Congo River across from Kinshasa. French is the official language. Much of the country is covered by dense equatorial rainforest.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo
text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a large country in Central Africa, with Kinshasa as its capital. French is the official language. The Congo River, one of the world's deepest, flows through vast rainforests that form part of the Congo Basin.

title: Costa Rica
text: Costa Rica is a country in Central America, with San Jose as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has coastlines on the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean, is known for rich biodiversity, rainforests, and volcanoes, and abolished its standing army in 1948.

title: Croatia
text: Croatia is a country in Southeastern Europe, with Zagreb as its capital. Croatian is the official language. It has a long, island-studded coastline on the Adriatic Sea and is known for historic cities such as Dubrovnik and Split.

title: Cuba
text: Cuba is the largest island nation in the Caribbean, with Havana as its capital. Spanish is the official language. Located south of Florida, it is known for its colonial architecture, music, and tobacco and sugar cultivation.

title: Cyprus
text: Cyprus is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean Sea, with Nicosia as its capital. Greek and Turkish are official languages. The island has been politically divided since 1974, and Nicosia is the world's last divided capital.

title: Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic, also called Czechia, is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with Prague as its capital. Czech is the official language. It comprises the historic regions of Bohemia, Moravia, and Silesia and is known for medieval castles and Gothic architecture.

title: Denmark
text: Denmark is a Nordic country in Northern Europe, with Copenhagen as its capital. Danish is the official language. It comprises the Jutland peninsula and many islands and borders the North and Baltic Seas. The autonomous territories of Greenland and the Faroe Islands belong to the kingdom.

title: Djibouti
text: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa, with Djibouti City as its capital. French and Arabic are official languages. It sits at the strategic Bab-el-Mandeb strait, where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden.

title: Dominica
text: Dominica is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, part of the Lesser Antilles, with Roseau as its capital. English is the official language. Known as the Nature Isle, it is mountainous and volcanic with rainforests and hot springs.

title: Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern part of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, with Santo Domingo as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It shares the island with Haiti and is known for its beaches and colonial history.

title: Ecuador
text: Ecuador is a country on the equator in northwestern South America, with Quito as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It borders the Pacific Ocean and includes the Galapagos Islands, famous for their unique wildlife, and the Andes run through its center.

title: Egypt
text: Egypt is a country linking northeast Africa with the Middle East, with Cairo as its capital. Arabic is the official language. The Nile River flows through the desert, and it is home to the ancient Pyramids of Giza and the Great Sphinx. The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

title: El Salvador
text: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America, with San Salvador as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has a Pacific coastline and a volcanic landscape, and is the only Central American nation without a Caribbean coast.

title: Equatorial Guinea
text: Equatorial Guinea is a country in Central Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Malabo as its capital, located on the island of Bioko. Spanish, French, and Portuguese are official languages. It comprises a mainland region and several islands.

title: Eritrea
text: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea, with Asmara as its capital. Tigrinya, Arabic, and English are widely used. Its capital is noted for Italian-influenced modernist architecture, and it borders the Danakil Depression.

title: Estonia
text: Estonia is a Baltic country in Northern Europe, with Tallinn as its capital. Estonian is the official language. It borders the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Finland and is known for its medieval old town and advanced digital government.

title: Eswatini
text: Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, is a small landlocked kingdom in Southern Africa, with Mbabane as its administrative capital and Lobamba as its royal and legislative capital. Swazi and English are official languages. It is one of the world's few remaining absolute monarchies.

title: Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa, with Addis Ababa as its capital, which hosts the African Union. Amharic is a widely used official language. It is one of the oldest nations, home to the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and the Ethiopian Highlands.

title: Fiji
text: Fiji is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean, with Suva as its capital, located on the island of Viti Levu. English, Fijian, and Hindi are official languages. It is an archipelago of hundreds of volcanic islands and coral reefs.

title: Finland
text: Finland is a Nordic country in Northern Europe, with Helsinki as its capital. Finnish and Swedish are official languages. Known as the land of thousands of lakes, it borders the Baltic Sea and features vast forests and the northern Lapland region.

title: France
text: France is a country in Western Europe, with Paris as its capital. French is the official language. It borders the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, and is known for the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, vineyards, and the Alps and Pyrenees mountains.

title: Gabon
text: Gabon is a country in Central Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Libreville as its capital. French is the official language. It lies on the equator and is heavily forested, with about a tenth of its land set aside as national parks.

title: Gambia
text: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa, with Banjul as its capital. English is the official language. It is a narrow nation surrounding the Gambia River and is nearly enclosed by Senegal, with a short Atlantic coastline.

title: Georgia
text: Georgia is a country in the South Caucasus region at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, with Tbilisi as its capital. Georgian is the official language, written in its own unique alphabet. It borders the Black Sea and features the Caucasus Mountains.

title: Germany
text: Germany is a country in Central Europe, with Berlin as its capital. German is the official language. It borders the North and Baltic Seas, is drained by the Rhine and Danube rivers, and is known for the Black Forest, Bavarian Alps, and historic cities.

title: Ghana
text: Ghana is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Accra as its capital. English is the official language. It was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence and is known for Lake Volta, one of the world's largest reservoirs.

title: Greece
text: Greece is a country in Southeastern Europe, with Athens as its capital. Greek is the official language. Bordering the Aegean, Ionian, and Mediterranean Seas, it comprises a mainland and thousands of islands and is regarded as the birthplace of Western democracy.

title: Grenada
text: Grenada is an island nation in the southeastern Caribbean, with Saint George's as its capital. English is the official language. Known as the Spice Isle, it is a leading producer of nutmeg and mace.

title: Guatemala
text: Guatemala is a country in Central America, with Guatemala City as its capital. Spanish is the official language, alongside many Mayan languages. It has coastlines on both the Pacific and Caribbean and contains volcanoes and ancient Maya ruins such as Tikal.

title: Guinea
text: Guinea is a country in West Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Conakry as its capital. French is the official language. Several major West African rivers, including the Niger, rise in its highlands, and it holds large bauxite reserves.

title: Guinea-Bissau
text: Guinea-Bissau is a country in West Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Bissau as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. Its territory includes the Bijagos Archipelago, a group of low-lying islands and mangroves.

title: Guyana
text: Guyana is a country on the northern coast of South America, with Georgetown as its capital. English is the official language. Culturally linked to the Caribbean, it features dense rainforest and the towering Kaieteur Falls.

title: Haiti
text: Haiti occupies the western part of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, with Port-au-Prince as its capital. French and Haitian Creole are official languages. It shares the island with the Dominican Republic and was the first independent Black republic.

title: Honduras
text: Honduras is a country in Central America, with Tegucigalpa as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has a long Caribbean coastline and a short Pacific one, and is home to the ancient Maya site of Copan.

title: Hungary
text: Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with Budapest as its capital. Hungarian is the official language. The Danube River divides the capital into Buda and Pest, and the country contains Lake Balaton, one of Central Europe's largest lakes.

title: Iceland
text: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic Ocean, with Reykjavik as its capital. Icelandic is the official language. It is a volcanic island known for geysers, glaciers, hot springs, and the northern lights, and sits atop the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

title: India
text: India is a large country in South Asia, with New Delhi as its capital. Hindi and English serve official functions among many languages. It borders the Indian Ocean, Arabian Sea, and Bay of Bengal, and is home to the Taj Mahal, the Ganges River, and part of the Himalayas.

title: Indonesia
text: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago, spanning Southeast Asia and Oceania, with Jakarta as its capital. Indonesian is the official language. It comprises thousands of islands, including Java, Sumatra, and Bali, and lies along the volcanic Ring of Fire.

title: Iran
text: Iran is a country in Western Asia, with Tehran as its capital. Persian, or Farsi, is the official language. It borders the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, features high plateaus and deserts, and is heir to the ancient Persian civilization.

title: Iraq
text: Iraq is a country in Western Asia, with Baghdad as its capital. Arabic and Kurdish are official languages. The Tigris and Euphrates rivers flow through it, and the region of Mesopotamia between them is often called the cradle of civilization.

title: Ireland
text: Ireland is an island country in Northwestern Europe, with Dublin as its capital. Irish and English are official languages. It occupies most of the island of Ireland, is known for green landscapes, and lies in the Atlantic Ocean west of Great Britain.

title: Israel
text: Israel is a country in Western Asia on the eastern Mediterranean coast, with Jerusalem as its proclaimed capital. Hebrew is the official language. It contains sites sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, and borders the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth's land surface.

title: Italy
text: Italy is a country in Southern Europe shaped like a boot, with Rome as its capital. Italian is the official language. It extends into the Mediterranean Sea and is known for the Colosseum, Venice's canals, the Leaning Tower of Pisa, and the Alps in the north.

title: Ivory Coast
text: Ivory Coast, or Cote d'Ivoire, is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Yamoussoukro as its official capital and Abidjan as its largest city. French is the official language. It is a leading producer of cocoa.

title: Jamaica
text: Jamaica is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea, with Kingston as its capital. English is the official language. Known for reggae music and Blue Mountain coffee, it lies south of Cuba and features tropical beaches and mountains.

title: Japan
text: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, with Tokyo as its capital. Japanese is the official language. It comprises a chain of islands in the Pacific Ocean, lies on the volcanic Ring of Fire, and is famous for Mount Fuji, cherry blossoms, and high-speed rail.

title: Jordan
text: Jordan is a country in Western Asia, with Amman as its capital. Arabic is the official language. Largely arid, it is home to the ancient rock-cut city of Petra and borders the Dead Sea, and has a very short coastline on the Red Sea at Aqaba.

title: Kazakhstan
text: Kazakhstan is a large landlocked country spanning Central Asia and Eastern Europe, with Astana as its capital. Kazakh and Russian are widely used. It is the world's largest landlocked country and features vast steppe grasslands and a Caspian Sea shoreline.

title: Kenya
text: Kenya is a country in East Africa on the Indian Ocean, with Nairobi as its capital. Swahili and English are official languages. The equator crosses it, and it is famous for wildlife safaris in the Maasai Mara and the Great Rift Valley. Mount Kenya is its highest peak.

title: Kiribati
text: Kiribati is an island nation in the central Pacific Ocean, with Tarawa as its capital. English and Gilbertese are used. It comprises low-lying coral atolls straddling the equator and the International Date Line, spread across a vast ocean area.

title: North Korea
text: North Korea, officially the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, is a country in East Asia, with Pyongyang as its capital. Korean is the official language. It occupies the northern half of the Korean Peninsula and borders China, Russia, and South Korea.

title: South Korea
text: South Korea, officially the Republic of Korea, is a country in East Asia, with Seoul as its capital. Korean is the official language. It occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula, bordered by the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan, and is known for its technology industry.

title: Kosovo
text: Kosovo is a partially recognized country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Pristina as its capital. Albanian and Serbian are official languages. It is landlocked and mountainous and declared independence from Serbia in 2008.

title: Kuwait
text: Kuwait is a country in Western Asia at the head of the Persian Gulf, with Kuwait City as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It is a small, oil-rich nation with a largely desert landscape and a strategic coastal position.

title: Kyrgyzstan
text: Kyrgyzstan is a landlocked country in Central Asia, with Bishkek as its capital. Kyrgyz and Russian are official languages. It is dominated by the Tian Shan mountains and contains Lake Issyk-Kul, one of the world's largest and deepest mountain lakes.

title: Laos
text: Laos is a landlocked country in Southeast Asia, with Vientiane as its capital. Lao is the official language. The Mekong River forms much of its border, and it is known for Buddhist temples and the historic town of Luang Prabang.

title: Latvia
text: Latvia is a Baltic country in Northern Europe, with Riga as its capital. Latvian is the official language. It borders the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Riga and is known for its Art Nouveau architecture and extensive forests.

title: Lebanon
text: Lebanon is a country in Western Asia on the eastern Mediterranean coast, with Beirut as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It is known for its mountains, ancient Phoenician cities, and cedar trees, which appear on its national flag.

title: Lesotho
text: Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, with Maseru as its capital. Sesotho and English are official languages. Known as the Kingdom in the Sky, it is the only country lying entirely above 1,000 metres in elevation.

title: Liberia
text: Liberia is a country in West Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Monrovia as its capital. English is the official language. Founded in the 19th century by freed American slaves, it is the oldest modern republic in Africa.

title: Libya
text: Libya is a country in North Africa on the Mediterranean coast, with Tripoli as its capital. Arabic is the official language. Most of its territory lies within the Sahara Desert, and it holds significant oil reserves.

title: Liechtenstein
text: Liechtenstein is a tiny landlocked microstate in Central Europe between Switzerland and Austria, with Vaduz as its capital. German is the official language. Situated in the Alps along the Rhine, it is a principality known for finance and mountain scenery.

title: Lithuania
text: Lithuania is a Baltic country in Northern Europe, with Vilnius as its capital. Lithuanian is the official language. It borders the Baltic Sea and is known for its baroque old town and a history as a large medieval grand duchy.

title: Luxembourg
text: Luxembourg is a small landlocked country in Western Europe, with Luxembourg City as its capital. Luxembourgish, French, and German are official languages. A grand duchy, it is a founding member of the European Union and a major financial center.

title: Madagascar
text: Madagascar is a large island nation in the Indian Ocean off the southeast coast of Africa, with Antananarivo as its capital. Malagasy and French are official languages. Isolated for millions of years, it hosts unique wildlife, including lemurs and baobab trees.

title: Malawi
text: Malawi is a landlocked country in Southeastern Africa, with Lilongwe as its capital. English and Chichewa are official languages. It is dominated by Lake Malawi, one of Africa's largest lakes, which teems with colorful fish.

title: Malaysia
text: Malaysia is a country in Southeast Asia divided between the Malay Peninsula and the island of Borneo, with Kuala Lumpur as its capital. Malay is the official language. It borders the South China Sea and is known for rainforests and the Petronas Towers.

title: Maldives
text: The Maldives is an island nation in the Indian Ocean southwest of India, with Male as its capital. Dhivehi is the official language. It is a chain of low-lying coral atolls and is one of the world's lowest-lying countries, renowned for luxury resorts.

title: Mali
text: Mali is a large landlocked country in West Africa, with Bamako as its capital. French is the official language. The Niger River flows through it, and its northern regions extend into the Sahara. The historic city of Timbuktu lies within its borders.

title: Malta
text: Malta is a small island nation in the central Mediterranean Sea south of Sicily, with Valletta as its capital. Maltese and English are official languages. It is an archipelago known for its ancient temples, fortified cities, and strategic maritime history.

title: Marshall Islands
text: The Marshall Islands is an island nation in the central Pacific Ocean, with Majuro as its capital. Marshallese and English are used. It comprises low-lying coral atolls and is known historically for nuclear testing at Bikini Atoll.

title: Mauritania
text: Mauritania is a country in Northwest Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Nouakchott as its capital. Arabic is the official language. Most of its territory lies within the Sahara Desert, bridging the Maghreb and West Africa.

title: Mauritius
text: Mauritius is an island nation in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, with Port Louis as its capital. English is used officially, alongside French and Creole. A volcanic island, it was the only known home of the extinct dodo bird.

title: Mexico
text: Mexico is a country in North America, with Mexico City as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It borders the Pacific Ocean, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Caribbean Sea, and is home to ancient Maya and Aztec ruins such as Chichen Itza.

title: Micronesia
text: The Federated States of Micronesia is an island nation in the western Pacific Ocean, with Palikir as its capital, on the island of Pohnpei. English is the official language. It comprises many islands spread across a vast ocean expanse.

title: Moldova
text: Moldova is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe between Romania and Ukraine, with Chisinau as its capital. Romanian is the official language. It is known for its rolling farmland and extensive vineyards and wine production.

title: Monaco
text: Monaco is a tiny city-state on the Mediterranean coast of Western Europe, surrounded by France, with Monaco as its capital city. French is the official language. Famous for its casino in Monte Carlo and the Formula One Grand Prix, it is one of the world's smallest countries.

title: Mongolia
text: Mongolia is a large landlocked country in East Asia between Russia and China, with Ulaanbaatar as its capital. Mongolian is the official language. It is known for the vast Gobi Desert, sweeping steppe grasslands, and a nomadic herding tradition.

title: Montenegro
text: Montenegro is a country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Podgorica as its capital. Montenegrin is the official language. It has a rugged Adriatic coastline and mountainous interior, including the dramatic Bay of Kotor.

title: Morocco
text: Morocco is a country in North Africa, with Rabat as its capital. Arabic and Berber are official languages. It has coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, features the Atlas Mountains, and the Sahara lies to its south.

title: Mozambique
text: Mozambique is a country in Southeastern Africa on the Indian Ocean, with Maputo as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It has a long coastline along the Mozambique Channel, facing the island of Madagascar.

title: Myanmar
text: Myanmar, also known as Burma, is a country in Southeast Asia, with Naypyidaw as its capital. Burmese is the official language. It borders the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea, and is known for its many gilded Buddhist pagodas, including Shwedagon in Yangon.

title: Namibia
text: Namibia is a country in Southern Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Windhoek as its capital. English is the official language. It contains the ancient Namib Desert, which gives the country its name, and the arid Skeleton Coast.

title: Nauru
text: Nauru is a tiny island nation in the central Pacific Ocean, one of the world's smallest countries, with no official capital though Yaren is the seat of government. Nauruan and English are used. It is a raised coral island once rich in phosphate.

title: Nepal
text: Nepal is a landlocked country in South Asia in the Himalayas, with Kathmandu as its capital. Nepali is the official language. It contains eight of the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest, the highest mountain on Earth, on its border with China.

title: Netherlands
text: The Netherlands is a country in Northwestern Europe, with Amsterdam as its capital and The Hague as its seat of government. Dutch is the official language. Much of the land is below sea level and protected by dikes, and it is known for canals, windmills, and tulips.

title: New Zealand
text: New Zealand is an island nation in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, with Wellington as its capital. English and Maori are official languages. It comprises two main islands, is known for dramatic landscapes, glaciers, and fjords, and lies far from other landmasses.

title: Nicaragua
text: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America, with Managua as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has Pacific and Caribbean coastlines and contains Lake Nicaragua, the largest lake in Central America, dotted with volcanoes.

title: Niger
text: Niger is a large landlocked country in West Africa, with Niamey as its capital. French is the official language. Much of its territory lies within the Sahara Desert, and it is named after the Niger River that flows through its southwest.

title: Nigeria
text: Nigeria is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Abuja as its capital. English is the official language. It is the most populous country in Africa, and the Niger and Benue rivers meet within its borders.

title: North Macedonia
text: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Skopje as its capital. Macedonian is the official language. It is mountainous and shares Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, with Albania.

title: Norway
text: Norway is a Nordic country in Northern Europe, with Oslo as its capital. Norwegian is the official language. Its long coastline along the Atlantic Ocean is cut by deep fjords, and northern regions offer views of the midnight sun and northern lights.

title: Oman
text: Oman is a country on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, with Muscat as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It has coastlines on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman and guards the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

title: Pakistan
text: Pakistan is a country in South Asia, with Islamabad as its capital. Urdu and English serve official functions. It borders the Arabian Sea, is drained by the Indus River, and contains K2, the second-highest mountain in the world, in the Karakoram range.

title: Palau
text: Palau is an island nation in the western Pacific Ocean, with Ngerulmud as its capital. Palauan and English are official languages. It is an archipelago known for its Rock Islands, coral reefs, and world-class diving.

title: Panama
text: Panama is a country in Central America connecting to South America, with Panama City as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It is home to the Panama Canal, which links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and shortens global shipping routes.

title: Papua New Guinea
text: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and nearby islands in the southwestern Pacific, with Port Moresby as its capital. English, Tok Pisin, and Hiri Motu are official. It is one of the most linguistically diverse countries on Earth.

title: Paraguay
text: Paraguay is a landlocked country in central South America, with Asuncion as its capital. Spanish and Guarani are official languages. The Paraguay River divides the country, and it shares the Itaipu Dam, a major hydroelectric project, with Brazil.

title: Peru
text: Peru is a country in western South America, with Lima as its capital. Spanish and Quechua are official languages. It borders the Pacific Ocean, contains part of the Amazon rainforest and the Andes, and is home to the ancient Inca city of Machu Picchu.

title: Philippines
text: The Philippines is an archipelago nation in Southeast Asia, with Manila as its capital. Filipino and English are official languages. It comprises thousands of islands in the Pacific Ocean and South China Sea and lies along the volcanic Ring of Fire.

title: Poland
text: Poland is a country in Central Europe, with Warsaw as its capital. Polish is the official language. It borders the Baltic Sea, features the Tatra Mountains in the south, and is crossed by the Vistula River. Krakow preserves its medieval heritage.

title: Portugal
text: Portugal is a country in Southwestern Europe on the Iberian Peninsula, with Lisbon as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It faces the Atlantic Ocean and includes the Azores and Madeira archipelagos, and has a long seafaring history.

title: Qatar
text: Qatar is a country occupying a peninsula on the Persian Gulf in Western Asia, with Doha as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It is a small, oil- and gas-rich nation with a largely desert landscape.

title: Romania
text: Romania is a country in Southeastern Europe, with Bucharest as its capital. Romanian is the official language. It borders the Black Sea, is crossed by the Carpathian Mountains and the Danube, and includes the Transylvania region famed for its castles.

title: Russia
text: Russia is the largest country in the world by area, spanning Eastern Europe and northern Asia, with Moscow as its capital. Russian is the official language. It stretches across eleven time zones and contains Lake Baikal, the deepest lake on Earth, and vast Siberian forests.

title: Rwanda
text: Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa's Great Lakes region, with Kigali as its capital. Kinyarwanda, French, English, and Swahili are official languages. Known as the land of a thousand hills, it is home to endangered mountain gorillas.

title: Saint Kitts and Nevis
text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a two-island nation in the Caribbean, the smallest sovereign state in the Americas, with Basseterre as its capital. English is the official language. It lies in the Lesser Antilles and features volcanic peaks.

title: Saint Lucia
text: Saint Lucia is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, with Castries as its capital. English is the official language. It is known for the twin volcanic peaks called the Pitons, which rise dramatically from the sea.

title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
text: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, with Kingstown as its capital. English is the official language. It comprises the main island of Saint Vincent and a chain of smaller Grenadine islands.

title: Samoa
text: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean, with Apia as its capital. Samoan and English are official languages. It comprises two main volcanic islands and is a center of Polynesian culture.

title: San Marino
text: San Marino is a tiny landlocked microstate surrounded by Italy, with the City of San Marino as its capital. Italian is the official language. Perched on Mount Titano, it claims to be one of the world's oldest surviving republics.

title: Sao Tome and Principe
text: Sao Tome and Principe is a small island nation in the Gulf of Guinea off Central Africa, with Sao Tome as its capital. Portuguese is the official language. It is a volcanic archipelago straddling the equator, known for cocoa production.

title: Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia is a large country occupying most of the Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia, with Riyadh as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It contains the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, and much of its interior is desert, including the vast Rub' al Khali.

title: Senegal
text: Senegal is a country in West Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Dakar as its capital, the westernmost point of mainland Africa. French is the official language. It nearly surrounds the Gambia and is known for its music and vibrant culture.

title: Serbia
text: Serbia is a landlocked country in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with Belgrade as its capital. Serbian is the official language, written in Cyrillic. The Danube River flows through it, and Belgrade sits where the Sava meets the Danube.

title: Seychelles
text: Seychelles is an island nation in the Indian Ocean northeast of Madagascar, with Victoria as its capital. Seychellois Creole, English, and French are official. It comprises many granite and coral islands and is known for pristine beaches and unique wildlife.

title: Sierra Leone
text: Sierra Leone is a country in West Africa on the Atlantic coast, with Freetown as its capital. English is the official language. Its name means Lion Mountains, and it has a large natural harbour and reserves of diamonds.

title: Singapore
text: Singapore is an island city-state in Southeast Asia at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, with Singapore as its capital. English, Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil are official. A major global port and financial hub, it sits along the strategic Strait of Malacca.

title: Slovakia
text: Slovakia is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with Bratislava as its capital. Slovak is the official language. It is mountainous, featuring the High Tatras, and the Danube River flows past its capital near the Austrian border.

title: Slovenia
text: Slovenia is a country in Central Europe, with Ljubljana as its capital. Slovene is the official language. It has a short Adriatic coastline, includes part of the Julian Alps, and features the scenic Lake Bled with its island church.

title: Solomon Islands
text: The Solomon Islands is an archipelago nation in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, with Honiara as its capital, on the island of Guadalcanal. English is the official language. It comprises many volcanic islands and was a major theater of World War II.

title: Somalia
text: Somalia is a country in the Horn of Africa, with Mogadishu as its capital. Somali and Arabic are official languages. It has the longest coastline on mainland Africa, along the Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden.

title: South Africa
text: South Africa is a country at the southern tip of Africa, with three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein. It recognizes eleven official languages. It borders the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, meeting at the Cape of Good Hope, and is known for wildlife and Table Mountain.

title: South Sudan
text: South Sudan is a landlocked country in East-Central Africa, with Juba as its capital. English is the official language. It became the world's newest widely recognized nation in 2011 and contains the vast Sudd wetland of the White Nile.

title: Spain
text: Spain is a country on the Iberian Peninsula in Southwestern Europe, with Madrid as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It has Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines, includes the Balearic and Canary Islands, and is known for flamenco, the Alhambra, and Gaudi's architecture.

title: Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka is an island nation in the Indian Ocean south of India, with Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte as its official capital and Colombo as its largest city. Sinhala and Tamil are official languages. It is known for tea plantations, ancient temples, and beaches.

title: Sudan
text: Sudan is a large country in Northeast Africa, with Khartoum as its capital, where the Blue and White Nile rivers meet. Arabic and English are official languages. It borders the Red Sea and contains ancient pyramids built by the Kingdom of Kush.

title: Suriname
text: Suriname is the smallest sovereign country in South America, with Paramaribo as its capital. Dutch is the official language. Located on the northern coast, it is heavily forested and culturally diverse, blending South American and Caribbean influences.

title: Sweden
text: Sweden is a Nordic country in Northern Europe, with Stockholm as its capital, built across fourteen islands. Swedish is the official language. It borders the Baltic Sea, features vast forests and lakes, and extends into the Arctic in the north.

title: Switzerland
text: Switzerland is a landlocked country in Central Europe, with Bern as its capital. German, French, Italian, and Romansh are official languages. Famous for the Alps, including the Matterhorn, it is known for neutrality, banking, chocolate, and precision watchmaking.

title: Syria
text: Syria is a country in Western Asia on the eastern Mediterranean coast, with Damascus as its capital, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. Arabic is the official language. It contains ancient sites such as Palmyra and Aleppo.

title: Taiwan
text: Taiwan is an island in East Asia off the coast of mainland China, with Taipei as its capital. Mandarin Chinese is the primary language. It faces the Taiwan Strait and the Pacific Ocean and is known for its technology industry and mountainous interior.

title: Tajikistan
text: Tajikistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia, with Dushanbe as its capital. Tajik is the official language. It is dominated by the high Pamir Mountains, sometimes called the Roof of the World, and is the most mountainous nation in Central Asia.

title: Tanzania
text: Tanzania is a country in East Africa on the Indian Ocean, with Dodoma as its capital and Dar es Salaam as its largest city. Swahili and English are official languages. It is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa, the Serengeti, and the island of Zanzibar.

title: Thailand
text: Thailand is a country in Southeast Asia, with Bangkok as its capital. Thai is the official language. It borders the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand, is known for ornate Buddhist temples and beaches, and was never formally colonized by a European power.

title: Timor-Leste
text: Timor-Leste, also called East Timor, occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor in Southeast Asia, with Dili as its capital. Portuguese and Tetum are official languages. It borders the Timor Sea and gained independence in 2002.

title: Togo
text: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, with Lome as its capital. French is the official language. It stretches inland from a short Atlantic coastline through hills and savanna.

title: Tonga
text: Tonga is a Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific Ocean, with Nuku'alofa as its capital. Tongan and English are official languages. It is an archipelago of many islands and is the last remaining Polynesian monarchy.

title: Trinidad and Tobago
text: Trinidad and Tobago is a twin-island nation off the coast of Venezuela in the southern Caribbean, with Port of Spain as its capital. English is the official language. It is the birthplace of calypso, steelpan music, and Carnival, and holds oil and gas reserves.

title: Tunisia
text: Tunisia is a country in North Africa on the Mediterranean coast, with Tunis as its capital. Arabic is the official language. The northernmost country in Africa, it contains the ruins of ancient Carthage and reaches into the Sahara in the south.

title: Turkey
text: Turkey, officially Turkiye, is a country straddling Eastern Europe and Western Asia, with Ankara as its capital. Turkish is the official language. Istanbul spans two continents across the Bosphorus, and the country borders the Black, Aegean, and Mediterranean Seas.

title: Turkmenistan
text: Turkmenistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia, with Ashgabat as its capital. Turkmen is the official language. Most of its territory is covered by the Karakum Desert, and it borders the Caspian Sea to the west.

title: Tuvalu
text: Tuvalu is a tiny island nation in the Pacific Ocean, one of the world's smallest and least populous countries, with Funafuti as its capital. Tuvaluan and English are used. It comprises low-lying coral atolls vulnerable to rising seas.

title: Uganda
text: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, with Kampala as its capital. English and Swahili are official languages. It lies on the equator, borders Lake Victoria, and contains part of the source of the Nile River. It is known for mountain gorillas.

title: Ukraine
text: Ukraine is a large country in Eastern Europe, with Kyiv as its capital. Ukrainian is the official language. It borders the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, features fertile plains known as the steppe, and is crossed by the Dnieper River.

title: United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates in Western Asia on the Persian Gulf, with Abu Dhabi as its capital. Arabic is the official language. Dubai is its best-known city, and much of the country is desert along a strategic coast.

title: United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom is a country in Northwestern Europe comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, with London as its capital. English is the main language. An island nation in the Atlantic, it is separated from mainland Europe by the English Channel.

title: United States
text: The United States is a large country in North America, with Washington, D.C. as its capital. English is the predominant language. It stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific, includes Alaska and Hawaii, and features the Grand Canyon, the Rocky Mountains, and the Mississippi River.

title: Uruguay
text: Uruguay is a country in southeastern South America, with Montevideo as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It lies on the Atlantic coast at the mouth of the Rio de la Plata and is known for its beaches, grasslands, and cattle ranching.

title: Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan is a doubly landlocked country in Central Asia, with Tashkent as its capital. Uzbek is the official language. It lies along the historic Silk Road and contains the fabled cities of Samarkand and Bukhara with their tiled Islamic architecture.

title: Vanuatu
text: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean, with Port Vila as its capital. Bislama, English, and French are official languages. It is a volcanic archipelago in Melanesia known for active volcanoes and diverse traditional cultures.

title: Vatican City
text: Vatican City is the world's smallest sovereign state, an enclave within Rome, Italy, with Vatican City as its own territory. Italian and Latin are used. It is the spiritual and administrative center of the Roman Catholic Church and home to St. Peter's Basilica.

title: Venezuela
text: Venezuela is a country on the northern coast of South America, with Caracas as its capital. Spanish is the official language. It borders the Caribbean Sea, contains part of the Orinoco River basin, and is home to Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

title: Vietnam
text: Vietnam is a country in Southeast Asia, with Hanoi as its capital. Vietnamese is the official language. It has a long coastline on the South China Sea, is crossed by the Mekong and Red River deltas, and is known for Ha Long Bay's limestone islands.

title: Yemen
text: Yemen is a country on the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia, with Sanaa as its capital. Arabic is the official language. It borders the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden and includes the Socotra archipelago, known for its unique plant life.

title: Zambia
text: Zambia is a landlocked country in Southern Africa, with Lusaka as its capital. English is the official language. It shares the mighty Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River with Zimbabwe and contains numerous national parks and wildlife reserves.

title: Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in Southern Africa, with Harare as its capital. English, Shona, and Ndebele are among its official languages. It shares Victoria Falls with Zambia and is named after the ancient stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe.

title: Landlocked countries
text: A landlocked country has no coastline and no direct access to the ocean. Examples include Switzerland, Nepal, Bolivia, Mongolia, and Ethiopia. There are more than forty landlocked nations, and a few, such as Uzbekistan, are even doubly landlocked.

title: Island nations
text: Island nations are countries made up entirely of one or more islands, with no land borders. Examples include Japan, Iceland, Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Cuba, and the many small island states of the Pacific and Caribbean.

title: Doubly landlocked states
text: A doubly landlocked country is surrounded only by other landlocked countries, so reaching the sea requires crossing at least two borders. The two examples in the world are Liechtenstein in Europe and Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

title: Countries spanning two continents
text: Some countries lie across two continents. Turkey and Russia span Europe and Asia, Egypt spans Africa and Asia across the Sinai, and the tiny nations near the Bosphorus and Caucasus sit at continental crossroads.

title: Microstates of Europe
text: Europe contains several microstates, among the smallest countries in the world. They include Vatican City, Monaco, San Marino, Liechtenstein, Andorra, and Malta, each with distinctive histories and compact territories.

title: Countries on the equator
text: The equator passes through several countries, including Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Kenya, Uganda, Indonesia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Nations on the equator typically have warm, tropical climates year-round.

title: Nordic countries
text: The Nordic countries are Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Iceland, along with associated territories. They share historical ties, high living standards, and cold northern climates, and several extend above the Arctic Circle.

title: Baltic states
text: The Baltic states are Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, three countries on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea in Northern Europe. Once part of the Soviet Union, they regained independence in the early 1990s and joined the European Union.

title: The Benelux countries
text: The Benelux is a grouping of three neighboring countries in Western Europe: Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg. They formed an early economic union that helped inspire the wider integration of the European Union.

title: Countries of the Arabian Peninsula
text: The Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia contains Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, and Kuwait. Largely arid, the region holds a major share of the world's oil and gas reserves.

title: Great Lakes region of Africa
text: The African Great Lakes region in East Africa surrounds lakes such as Victoria, Tanganyika, and Malawi. It includes countries such as Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Countries sharing the Amazon
text: The Amazon rainforest and river basin extend across several South American countries, including Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Venezuela, and Guyana. Brazil contains the largest portion of the forest.

title: Countries sharing the Alps
text: The Alpine mountain range is shared by several European countries, including France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, Germany, Slovenia, and Liechtenstein. The Alps shape the climate, rivers, and culture of the region.

title: Countries sharing the Sahara
text: The Sahara Desert stretches across northern Africa, touching countries such as Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Niger, Chad, Sudan, Mauritania, and Morocco. Its vast, arid expanse dominates much of the continent's north.

title: Countries sharing the Himalayas
text: The Himalayan mountain range spans several countries, including Nepal, India, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan. It contains the world's highest peaks and is the source of major rivers that sustain much of Asia.

title: Commonwealth realms
text: Several countries, including Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Jamaica, share the British monarch as their head of state as Commonwealth realms. They are independent nations linked by history and the wider Commonwealth.

title: Spanish-speaking countries
text: Spanish is the official or dominant language in Spain and most of Latin America, including Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Peru, and Chile. It is one of the most widely spoken first languages in the world.

title: Portuguese-speaking countries
text: Portuguese is the official language of Portugal, Brazil, Angola, Mozambique, and several other nations. Brazil is by far the most populous Portuguese-speaking country, and the language spans four continents.

title: French-speaking countries
text: French is an official language in France and many countries across Africa, such as Senegal, Ivory Coast, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as in Canada, Belgium, and Switzerland.

title: Arabic-speaking countries
text: Arabic is the official language across much of the Middle East and North Africa, including Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Morocco, and Algeria. It exists in a classical form and many spoken regional dialects.

title: Countries with multiple capitals
text: A few countries have more than one capital. South Africa has three, Bolivia and Eswatini split legislative and administrative roles, and the Netherlands distinguishes its constitutional capital from its seat of government.

title: Countries that changed their names
text: Several countries have changed their names over time. Examples include Myanmar, formerly Burma, Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, and Cabo Verde, and cities and nations have often renamed themselves after independence.

title: Newest widely recognized nation
text: South Sudan, which gained independence in 2011, is the world's newest widely recognized sovereign state. It separated from Sudan after a long conflict and is a landlocked country in East-Central Africa.

title: Transcontinental Russia
text: Russia is the largest country in the world by area and spans two continents, Europe and Asia, across the Ural Mountains. Stretching over eleven time zones, it borders both the Atlantic-linked seas and the Pacific Ocean.

title: Countries of the Caucasus
text: The Caucasus region between the Black and Caspian Seas contains Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan, at the crossroads of Europe and Asia. Mountainous and diverse, it has ancient cultures and many distinct languages.

title: Countries of Central Asia
text: Central Asia comprises Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan. All landlocked, they lie along the historic Silk Road and range from vast steppes and deserts to towering mountains.

title: Pacific island nations
text: The Pacific Ocean is dotted with small island nations such as Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Kiribati, and Tuvalu. Many consist of low coral atolls or volcanic islands and share rich seafaring cultures.

title: Caribbean island nations
text: The Caribbean Sea contains many island nations, including Cuba, Jamaica, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, the Bahamas, Barbados, and Trinidad and Tobago. They share warm climates and diverse, blended cultures.

title: Countries of the Horn of Africa
text: The Horn of Africa in Northeast Africa includes Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti. Jutting toward the Arabian Peninsula, the region controls access to the Red Sea and holds ancient civilizations.

title: Countries bordering the Mediterranean
text: Many countries border the Mediterranean Sea, including Spain, France, Italy, Greece, Turkey, Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, Algeria, and Morocco. They share warm climates and a long shared history of trade and culture.

title: Southernmost inhabited regions
text: The southernmost inhabited towns lie in southern Chile and Argentina in the region of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego. Beyond them stretches the cold Southern Ocean and the uninhabited continent of Antarctica.

title: Northernmost countries
text: The northernmost inhabited lands belong to countries such as Canada, Greenland, Norway, Russia, and the United States through Alaska. These Arctic regions endure long, dark winters and cold summers.

title: Countries entirely within another
text: A few countries are entirely surrounded by a single other country. Lesotho and, in a sense, San Marino and Vatican City are enclaves fully enclosed within South Africa and Italy respectively.

title: Highest capital cities
text: Some capital cities sit at very high elevations. La Paz in Bolivia and Quito in Ecuador are among the highest, set thousands of metres above sea level in the Andes, which affects their climate and the visitors who arrive there.

title: Most populous countries
text: The most populous countries in the world include India and China, each with well over a billion people, followed by nations such as the United States, Indonesia, and Pakistan. Together they hold a large share of humanity.

title: Largest countries by area
text: The largest countries by land area are Russia, Canada, China, the United States, and Brazil. Russia alone spans a vast portion of the Earth's land surface across northern Europe and Asia.

title: Paris, France
text: Paris, the capital of France, is known worldwide as a center of art, fashion, and cuisine. It sits on the Seine River and is home to the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and Notre-Dame Cathedral. It has long been called the City of Light.

title: London, England
text: London, the capital of the United Kingdom, lies on the River Thames. It is a global financial hub known for landmarks such as Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, the Tower of London, and the London Eye, and for its historic role as a center of the British Empire.

title: Rome, Italy
text: Rome, the capital of Italy, is often called the Eternal City. Once the heart of the Roman Empire, it contains ancient ruins such as the Colosseum and Roman Forum, as well as Vatican City, an independent state within its bounds.

title: Tokyo, Japan
text: Tokyo, the capital of Japan, is one of the world's largest metropolitan areas. It blends ultramodern skyscrapers, technology, and neon districts with historic temples and gardens, and serves as the country's political and economic center.

title: Beijing, China
text: Beijing, the capital of China, is a center of Chinese politics and culture. It is home to the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square, and the Temple of Heaven, and lies near sections of the Great Wall of China.

title: Moscow, Russia
text: Moscow, the capital of Russia, sits on the Moskva River. It is known for the Kremlin, the seat of Russian government, and the colorful onion domes of Saint Basil's Cathedral overlooking Red Square.

title: Washington, D.C., USA
text: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States, a planned city on the Potomac River. It houses the White House, the Capitol, and the Supreme Court, along with monuments and museums along the National Mall.

title: Cairo, Egypt
text: Cairo, the capital of Egypt, is one of the largest cities in Africa and the Arab world. It sits on the Nile River near the ancient Pyramids of Giza and is a historic center of Islamic learning and culture.

title: Berlin, Germany
text: Berlin, the capital of Germany, is known for its turbulent 20th-century history. Landmarks include the Brandenburg Gate and remnants of the Berlin Wall, which once divided the city, now reunited as a cultural and creative hub.

title: Madrid, Spain
text: Madrid, the capital of Spain, lies near the geographic center of the country. It is known for grand boulevards, the Prado Museum's art collection, the Royal Palace, and a vibrant nightlife and cafe culture.

title: Athens, Greece
text: Athens, the capital of Greece, is one of the world's oldest cities and the birthplace of democracy. It is dominated by the Acropolis, crowned by the ancient Parthenon temple dedicated to the goddess Athena.

title: Vienna, Austria
text: Vienna, the capital of Austria, sits on the Danube River and is renowned for its classical music heritage, associated with composers such as Mozart and Beethoven. It is known for imperial palaces, coffee houses, and grand architecture.

title: Amsterdam, Netherlands
text: Amsterdam, the capital of the Netherlands, is famed for its concentric canals, narrow gabled houses, and cycling culture. It hosts world-class museums including the Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum.

title: Brussels, Belgium
text: Brussels, the capital of Belgium, serves as the administrative center of the European Union. It is known for its Grand Place, historic guild houses, chocolate, waffles, and the small Manneken Pis statue.

title: Lisbon, Portugal
text: Lisbon, the capital of Portugal, is built on hills overlooking the Tagus River near the Atlantic. Known for its trams, tiled facades, and Fado music, it is one of the oldest cities in Western Europe.

title: Stockholm, Sweden
text: Stockholm, the capital of Sweden, is spread across fourteen islands where a lake meets the Baltic Sea. It is known for its well-preserved medieval old town, Gamla Stan, and its role in awarding the Nobel Prizes.

title: Oslo, Norway
text: Oslo, the capital of Norway, sits at the head of the Oslofjord. Surrounded by forests and hills, it is known for museums of Viking ships and polar exploration, and for modern architecture such as its waterfront opera house.

title: Copenhagen, Denmark
text: Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark, is known for its cycling culture, colorful harbor of Nyhavn, and the Little Mermaid statue. It is often ranked among the world's most livable cities.

title: Helsinki, Finland
text: Helsinki, the capital of Finland, lies on a peninsula on the Gulf of Finland. It is known for its design, modernist and neoclassical architecture, and its distinctive Lutheran cathedral overlooking the harbor.

title: Dublin, Ireland
text: Dublin, the capital of Ireland, sits at the mouth of the River Liffey. Rich in literary history, it is associated with writers such as James Joyce and is known for Trinity College, its Georgian architecture, and pub culture.

title: Warsaw, Poland
text: Warsaw, the capital of Poland, was largely rebuilt after World War II, including a faithful reconstruction of its historic Old Town. It sits on the Vistula River and is the country's political and economic center.

title: Prague, Czech Republic
text: Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic, is famed for its well-preserved medieval core, the Charles Bridge, Prague Castle, and the astronomical clock in its Old Town Square. It straddles the Vltava River.

title: Budapest, Hungary
text: Budapest, the capital of Hungary, is divided by the Danube into the hilly Buda and flat Pest sides. It is known for its thermal baths, the grand Parliament building, and the Chain Bridge linking the two halves.

title: Ankara, Turkey
text: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, located in the central Anatolian plateau. Chosen as capital in 1923, it is home to the mausoleum of Ataturk, the founder of modern Turkey, and serves as the nation's administrative center.

title: New Delhi, India
text: New Delhi is the capital of India, forming part of the larger Delhi metropolitan area. It contains government institutions, wide ceremonial avenues, and landmarks such as India Gate and the historic Red Fort in Old Delhi.

title: Bangkok, Thailand
text: Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, is known for ornate Buddhist temples such as Wat Arun, the Grand Palace, bustling markets, and vibrant street food. The Chao Phraya River winds through the city.

title: Jakarta, Indonesia
text: Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia, is a sprawling metropolis on the northwest coast of Java. A major commercial center, it blends colonial-era buildings with modern skyscrapers and faces challenges from congestion and subsidence.

title: Seoul, South Korea
text: Seoul, the capital of South Korea, sits on the Han River. It combines ancient palaces such as Gyeongbokgung with a dense modern skyline, and is a global center of technology and popular culture.

title: Canberra, Australia
text: Canberra is the capital of Australia, a planned city chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne. It houses Parliament House, the Australian War Memorial, and national museums around an artificial lake.

title: Ottawa, Canada
text: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, located in Ontario on the Ottawa River across from Quebec. It is home to the Gothic Revival Parliament buildings and reflects the country's bilingual English and French character.

title: Mexico City, Mexico
text: Mexico City, the capital of Mexico, is one of the largest cities in the Americas, built on the site of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan. It sits in a high valley and is known for its historic center, museums, and Aztec ruins.

title: Buenos Aires, Argentina
text: Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina, sits on the Rio de la Plata. Often called the Paris of South America for its European-style architecture, it is the birthplace of the tango and known for its lively cafe culture.

title: Brasilia, Brazil
text: Brasilia, the capital of Brazil, is a planned city inaugurated in 1960 and famed for its modernist architecture designed by Oscar Niemeyer. Laid out in the shape of an airplane, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Nairobi, Kenya
text: Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, is a major hub of East Africa. Unusually for a large city, it borders a national park where wildlife roams within sight of the skyline, and it serves as a regional business center.

title: Pretoria, South Africa
text: Pretoria is the administrative capital of South Africa, one of the country's three capitals. Known for its jacaranda trees that bloom purple in spring, it houses the Union Buildings, the seat of the national government.

title: Wellington, New Zealand
text: Wellington, the capital of New Zealand, sits at the southern tip of the North Island on a natural harbor. Known for its windy weather, arts scene, and cafe culture, it is a compact and hilly city.

title: Reykjavik, Iceland
text: Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland, is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state. Powered largely by geothermal energy, it serves as a base for exploring nearby volcanoes, geysers, and the northern lights.

title: Havana, Cuba
text: Havana, the capital of Cuba, is known for its well-preserved Spanish colonial architecture, vintage American cars, and lively music. Its historic center, Old Havana, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Lima, Peru
text: Lima, the capital of Peru, lies on the Pacific coast. Founded by Spanish conquistadors, its historic center preserves colonial churches and mansions, and the city is celebrated for its influential culinary scene.

title: Santiago, Chile
text: Santiago, the capital of Chile, sits in a valley surrounded by the snow-capped Andes. It is the country's cultural and financial center, known for its museums, parks, and nearby vineyards.

title: Bogota, Colombia
text: Bogota, the capital of Colombia, is a high-altitude city set on a plateau in the Andes. It is known for its historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, and a vibrant arts and coffee culture.

title: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
text: Kuala Lumpur, the capital of Malaysia, is known for the twin Petronas Towers, once the tallest buildings in the world. It blends Malay, Chinese, and Indian cultures and serves as a major Southeast Asian business hub.

title: Singapore City
text: Singapore is a city-state that serves as its own capital, known for cleanliness, greenery, and futuristic architecture such as Marina Bay Sands and the Gardens by the Bay. It is one of the world's busiest ports and financial centers.

title: Hanoi, Vietnam
text: Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam, is known for its centuries-old architecture blending French colonial and traditional Vietnamese styles. Its Old Quarter features narrow streets, temples, and the scenic Hoan Kiem Lake.

title: Manila, Philippines
text: Manila, the capital of the Philippines, lies on the shores of Manila Bay. A historic port, it contains the old walled city of Intramuros from the Spanish colonial era and serves as the country's political center.

title: Islamabad, Pakistan
text: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, a planned city built in the 1960s at the foot of the Margalla Hills. Known for its greenery and modern layout, it is home to the striking Faisal Mosque.

title: Dhaka, Bangladesh
text: Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, is one of the most densely populated cities in the world. Set on the Buriganga River, it is known for its Mughal-era architecture, colorful cycle rickshaws, and textile industry.

title: Tehran, Iran
text: Tehran, the capital of Iran, lies at the foot of the Alborz Mountains. The country's political and cultural center, it is known for its museums, palaces of former rulers, and bustling grand bazaar.

title: Baghdad, Iraq
text: Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, sits on the Tigris River. Once a leading center of learning during the Islamic Golden Age, it has a long and storied history stretching back over a millennium.

title: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
text: Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, is a modern desert metropolis and the country's political and financial heart. It features soaring skyscrapers alongside historic mud-brick districts such as Diriyah.

title: Abu Dhabi, UAE
text: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates, sitting on an island in the Persian Gulf. It is known for the grand Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, cultural institutions, and wealth from oil reserves.

title: Jerusalem
text: Jerusalem is a city sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, and is claimed as capital by Israel. Its walled Old City contains the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, and the Dome of the Rock.

title: Damascus, Syria
text: Damascus, the capital of Syria, is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Its old city preserves ancient walls, souks, and the historic Umayyad Mosque.

title: Amman, Jordan
text: Amman, the capital of Jordan, is a hilly city built across several hills in the desert highlands. It blends ancient Roman ruins, such as a well-preserved theater, with a modern, cosmopolitan character.

title: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
text: Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, is one of the highest capital cities in the world. It hosts the headquarters of the African Union and is a diplomatic center for the continent.

title: Accra, Ghana
text: Accra, the capital of Ghana, is a coastal city on the Gulf of Guinea. A lively commercial and cultural center, it is known for its markets, beaches, and monuments to Ghana's independence.

title: Nassau, Bahamas
text: Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, sits on New Providence Island. A major cruise and tourism hub, it is known for colonial architecture, beaches, and its history connected to piracy in the Caribbean.

title: Kabul, Afghanistan
text: Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan, lies in a high mountain valley along the Kabul River. A strategic city on ancient trade routes, it has served as a crossroads between Central and South Asia for centuries.

title: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
text: Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, is the coldest capital city in the world. Set on the steppe, it is the country's cultural and economic center and a gateway to Mongolia's vast nomadic landscapes.

title: Astana, Kazakhstan
text: Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, is a planned city on the steppe known for its futuristic architecture. It became the capital in 1997 and features distinctive modern landmarks rising from the plains.

title: Kyiv, Ukraine
text: Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine, set on the Dnieper River. One of the oldest cities in Eastern Europe, it is known for its gold-domed Orthodox churches, including the Saint Sophia Cathedral, and its historic role in Slavic culture.

title: Bratislava, Slovakia
text: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia, situated on the Danube River near the borders of Austria and Hungary. It is known for its compact old town, hilltop castle, and position as one of Europe's smaller capital cities.

title: Ljubljana, Slovenia
text: Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia, a green city crossed by the Ljubljanica River. It is known for its baroque and Art Nouveau architecture, a hilltop castle, and bridges designed by the architect Joze Plecnik.

title: Zagreb, Croatia
text: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, set in the country's north. It is known for its medieval upper town, Austro-Hungarian architecture, lively squares, and museums, and serves as the nation's cultural and political center.

title: Belgrade, Serbia
text: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, situated where the Sava River meets the Danube. One of the oldest cities in Europe, it is known for its riverside fortress, vibrant nightlife, and turbulent history at the crossroads of empires.

title: Sofia, Bulgaria
text: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria, lying at the foot of the Vitosha mountain. One of Europe's oldest cities, it blends Roman ruins, Ottoman mosques, and Orthodox churches, including the grand Alexander Nevsky Cathedral.

title: Bucharest, Romania
text: Bucharest is the capital of Romania, once nicknamed the Little Paris of the East for its elegant architecture. It is home to the enormous Palace of the Parliament, one of the largest administrative buildings in the world.

title: Tallinn, Estonia
text: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia, on the Baltic coast. It is celebrated for its exceptionally well-preserved medieval old town, with cobbled streets, defensive towers, and Gothic spires enclosed by ancient walls.

title: Riga, Latvia
text: Riga is the capital of Latvia, the largest city in the Baltic states. Set on the Daugava River, it is renowned for its rich collection of Art Nouveau architecture and its historic Hanseatic old town.

title: Vilnius, Lithuania
text: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania, known for its sprawling baroque old town, one of the largest in Eastern Europe. It features numerous churches and a rich blend of architectural styles reflecting its layered history.

title: Minsk, Belarus
text: Minsk is the capital of Belarus, largely rebuilt in a monumental Soviet style after World War II. It is known for its broad avenues, grand public squares, and well-ordered parks along the Svisloch River.

title: Chisinau, Moldova
text: Chisinau is the capital of Moldova, a green city known for its parks and tree-lined boulevards. It serves as the country's cultural and economic center and lies within a region famous for its vineyards.

title: Yerevan, Armenia
text: Yerevan is the capital of Armenia, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. Built largely of pink volcanic stone, it offers views of Mount Ararat and is a center of Armenian culture and history.

title: Tbilisi, Georgia
text: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, set in a valley on the Kura River. Known for its charming old town, sulfur bathhouses, and blend of European and Asian influences, it has long been a crossroads of trade and culture.

title: Baku, Azerbaijan
text: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the shore of the Caspian Sea. It combines a walled medieval old city with striking modern architecture, including the Flame Towers, and grew wealthy from its oil industry.
