title: Tashkent, Uzbekistan
text: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan and the largest city in Central Asia. A historic Silk Road hub rebuilt after an earthquake, it blends Soviet-era planning with Islamic monuments and bustling bazaars.

title: Almaty region, Kazakhstan
text: Almaty is the largest city and former capital of Kazakhstan, set against a backdrop of snow-capped mountains. A cultural and financial center, it is known for its tree-lined streets, parks, and nearby ski resorts.

title: Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan
text: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan, lying at the foot of the Tian Shan mountains. Known for its wide boulevards, Soviet-era architecture, and green spaces, it serves as the country's political and cultural center.

title: Colombo, Sri Lanka
text: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka, on the island's west coast. A busy port with a mix of colonial buildings, temples, and modern developments, it has long been a center of Indian Ocean trade.

title: Kathmandu, Nepal
text: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal, set in a valley in the Himalayas. It is renowned for its dense concentration of Hindu and Buddhist temples, ancient palace squares, and its role as a gateway to Everest trekking.

title: Naypyidaw, Myanmar
text: Naypyidaw is the purpose-built capital of Myanmar, established in 2005. Known for its exceptionally wide, often empty boulevards and spacious government complexes, it replaced Yangon as the seat of national government.

title: Vientiane, Laos
text: Vientiane is the capital of Laos, a quiet riverside city on the Mekong. Known for its Buddhist temples, French colonial architecture, and relaxed pace, it is one of Southeast Asia's smaller and calmer capitals.

title: Phnom Penh, Cambodia
text: Phnom Penh is the capital of Cambodia, where the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers meet. It is known for its Royal Palace, the Silver Pagoda, and its role in the country's recent history.

title: Ulaanbaatar overview
text: Ulaanbaatar, capital of Mongolia, sits in a valley on the Tuul River surrounded by mountains. As the country's only large city, it blends Soviet-era buildings, Buddhist monasteries, and the traditional round tents called gers.

title: Doha, Qatar
text: Doha is the capital of Qatar, a rapidly modernized city on the Persian Gulf. It is known for its futuristic skyline, the Museum of Islamic Art, and its ambitious development fueled by natural gas wealth.

title: Muscat, Oman
text: Muscat is the capital of Oman, set between rugged mountains and the Gulf of Oman. Known for its low-rise, whitewashed buildings, grand mosque, and historic forts, it preserves a distinctly traditional Arabian character.

title: Kuwait City overview
text: Kuwait City is the capital of Kuwait, a modern metropolis at the head of the Persian Gulf. It is known for its distinctive water towers, waterfront corniche, and wealth derived from the country's oil reserves.

title: Manama overview
text: Manama is the capital of Bahrain, a compact city on the Persian Gulf. A regional financial center, it blends modern towers with traditional souks and reflects the island's long history of trade and pearl diving.

title: Sanaa, Yemen
text: Sanaa is the capital of Yemen and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Its old city is famous for distinctive tower houses of rammed earth decorated with white geometric patterns.

title: Beirut overview
text: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon, a Mediterranean port city known for its resilience and cultural vibrancy. It blends ancient ruins, French-influenced architecture, and a lively arts and food scene.

title: Tunis overview
text: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia, blending a historic walled medina with French colonial avenues. Nearby lie the ruins of ancient Carthage, once a great Mediterranean power that rivaled Rome.

title: Algiers overview
text: Algiers is the capital of Algeria, a white-walled city rising in tiers above the Mediterranean. Its historic Casbah, a maze of narrow streets and Ottoman-era buildings, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Tripoli overview
text: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, an ancient port on the Mediterranean coast. Founded by the Phoenicians, it preserves Roman ruins and a historic medina alongside its role as the country's largest city.

title: Rabat overview
text: Rabat is the capital of Morocco, a coastal city on the Atlantic. Known for its historic medina, the unfinished Hassan Tower, and the Kasbah of the Udayas, it blends Islamic heritage with modern administration.

title: Khartoum overview
text: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, located where the Blue Nile and White Nile rivers join to form the main Nile. It serves as the country's political, cultural, and commercial center.

title: Dakar overview
text: Dakar is the capital of Senegal, set on a peninsula that forms the westernmost point of mainland Africa. A lively cultural hub, it is known for its music, markets, and historic Goree Island offshore.

title: Kampala overview
text: Kampala is the capital of Uganda, built across several hills near Lake Victoria. A bustling, green city, it serves as the country's commercial and cultural center and a gateway to Uganda's wildlife parks.

title: Kigali overview
text: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda, spread across scenic hills. Known for its notable cleanliness, orderliness, and safety, it has become a symbol of the country's recovery and development.

title: Dar es Salaam overview
text: Dar es Salaam is the largest city and commercial heart of Tanzania, a busy port on the Indian Ocean. Though the official capital is Dodoma, it remains the country's main economic and cultural center.

title: Harare overview
text: Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe, set on a high plateau. Known for its wide, tree-lined avenues and gardens, it serves as the nation's political and commercial center.

title: Windhoek overview
text: Windhoek is the capital of Namibia, located in the country's central highlands. A small, orderly city, it shows German colonial influences in its architecture and serves as a gateway to Namibia's deserts.

title: Gaborone overview
text: Gaborone is the capital of Botswana, a modern, planned city that grew rapidly after independence. It serves as the political and economic center of a country known for stable governance and wildlife tourism.

title: Antananarivo overview
text: Antananarivo is the capital of Madagascar, a hilly city with narrow winding streets and terraced rice paddies nearby. It blends French colonial and Malagasy influences and serves as the island nation's largest city.

title: Panama City overview
text: Panama City is the capital of Panama, a modern skyline rising beside the historic Casco Viejo district and the Pacific entrance to the Panama Canal. It is a major banking and shipping hub for the Americas.

title: San Jose overview
text: San Jose is the capital of Costa Rica, set in a central valley ringed by mountains. It serves as the country's cultural and economic center and a base for exploring its rainforests and volcanoes.

title: Quito overview
text: Quito is the capital of Ecuador, set high in the Andes near the equator. Its well-preserved colonial old town, one of the largest and best-preserved in the Americas, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Montevideo overview
text: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay, a coastal city on the Rio de la Plata. Known for its long waterfront promenade, historic old town, and relaxed atmosphere, it is the country's cultural and economic hub.

title: Asuncion overview
text: Asuncion is the capital of Paraguay, one of the oldest cities in South America, set on the Paraguay River. It serves as the political and cultural heart of the landlocked nation.

title: La Paz overview
text: La Paz is the administrative capital of Bolivia and the highest seat of government in the world, set in a dramatic canyon high in the Andes. Its steep streets are served by a network of aerial cable cars.

title: Caracas overview
text: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela, set in a valley near the Caribbean coast and backed by the Avila mountain. It is the country's political and cultural center.

title: Georgetown overview
text: Georgetown is the capital of Guyana, a coastal city known for its wooden colonial architecture and Dutch-built drainage canals. It serves as the country's main port and administrative center.

title: Santo Domingo overview
text: Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, is the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the Americas. Its colonial zone preserves the first cathedral and fortress built in the New World.

title: Kingston overview
text: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica, set on a natural harbor. The birthplace of much of the island's music, it is a center of reggae culture and home to sites associated with Bob Marley.

title: Port of Spain overview
text: Port of Spain is the capital of Trinidad and Tobago, known for its vibrant Carnival, steelpan music, and diverse culture. It serves as a commercial center in the southern Caribbean.

title: Suva overview
text: Suva is the capital of Fiji, a port city on the island of Viti Levu. The largest urban center in the South Pacific islands, it blends colonial buildings with a diverse, multicultural population.

title: Port Moresby overview
text: Port Moresby is the capital of Papua New Guinea, set on the Gulf of Papua. It serves as the gateway to one of the world's most culturally and biologically diverse nations.

title: Apia overview
text: Apia is the capital of Samoa, a port town on the island of Upolu. It preserves Polynesian traditions and colonial-era buildings and was the final home of the writer Robert Louis Stevenson.

title: Male overview
text: Male is the capital of the Maldives, one of the most densely populated cities in the world, packed onto a small coral island. It is the political and commercial hub of the low-lying island nation.

title: Thimphu overview
text: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan, one of the few capitals without traffic lights. Set in a Himalayan valley, it blends traditional Bhutanese architecture with Buddhist monasteries and government buildings.

title: New York City, USA
text: New York City is the largest city in the United States, spread across five boroughs at the mouth of the Hudson River. A global center of finance, media, and culture, it is known for the Statue of Liberty, Times Square, Central Park, and the skyscrapers of Manhattan.

title: Los Angeles, USA
text: Los Angeles is a sprawling city on the coast of Southern California, known as the center of the American film and television industry in Hollywood. It features beaches, mountains, and a car-oriented culture spread across a wide basin.

title: Chicago, USA
text: Chicago is a major city on the shore of Lake Michigan in the American Midwest. Known for its influential architecture and the birth of the skyscraper, it is a transportation and financial hub with a distinctive skyline.

title: San Francisco, USA
text: San Francisco is a hilly city on a peninsula in Northern California, known for the Golden Gate Bridge, cable cars, and Victorian houses. It anchors a region that is a global center of technology innovation.

title: Sydney, Australia
text: Sydney is the largest city in Australia, set around a spectacular natural harbor. It is famous for the sail-shaped Sydney Opera House and the Harbour Bridge, and for beaches such as Bondi.

title: Melbourne, Australia
text: Melbourne is a major city in southeastern Australia known for its arts, coffee culture, and sporting events, including the Australian Open tennis tournament. It is noted for its laneways, trams, and Victorian-era architecture.

title: Barcelona, Spain
text: Barcelona is a coastal city in the Catalonia region of Spain, known for the distinctive architecture of Antoni Gaudi, including the unfinished Sagrada Familia basilica. It combines Mediterranean beaches with a vibrant cultural scene.

title: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
text: Rio de Janeiro is a coastal city in Brazil famous for its beaches, Carnival celebrations, and the Christ the Redeemer statue atop Corcovado mountain. Sugarloaf Mountain rises dramatically above its harbor.

title: Mumbai, India
text: Mumbai is the largest city in India and its financial capital, located on the west coast. Home to the Bollywood film industry, it is known for colonial-era buildings, the Gateway of India, and a dense, bustling energy.

title: Shanghai, China
text: Shanghai is the largest city in China and a global financial center on the Yangtze River delta. Its skyline along the Bund contrasts colonial-era buildings with the futuristic towers of the Pudong district.

title: Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China on the Pearl River delta. Known for its dense skyline, busy harbor, and role as a global financial hub, it blends Chinese and British colonial influences.

title: Istanbul, Turkey
text: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey, straddling Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus strait. Formerly Constantinople, it is known for the Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, and the Grand Bazaar.

title: Dubai, UAE
text: Dubai is the largest city in the United Arab Emirates, known for ultramodern architecture, luxury shopping, and the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world. It has grown rapidly from a desert port into a global hub.

title: Cape Town, South Africa
text: Cape Town is a coastal city in South Africa at the foot of the flat-topped Table Mountain. One of the country's three capitals, it is known for its dramatic scenery, harbor, and the nearby Cape of Good Hope.

title: Toronto, Canada
text: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, on the shore of Lake Ontario. A diverse, multicultural metropolis, it is known for the CN Tower and serves as the country's financial and cultural center.

title: Vancouver, Canada
text: Vancouver is a coastal city in western Canada, set between the Pacific Ocean and the Coast Mountains. It is known for its natural beauty, mild climate, and Stanley Park, and consistently ranks among the world's most livable cities.

title: Milan, Italy
text: Milan is a major city in northern Italy, regarded as a global capital of fashion and design. It is home to the vast Gothic Milan Cathedral, the La Scala opera house, and Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper.

title: Venice, Italy
text: Venice is a city in northeastern Italy built across many small islands in a lagoon, famed for its canals, gondolas, and bridges. St. Mark's Square and Basilica lie at its heart, and it hosts a renowned annual film festival.

title: Munich, Germany
text: Munich is a major city in Bavaria, southern Germany, near the Alps. It is known for its Oktoberfest beer festival, historic squares, beer gardens, and its role as a center of engineering and industry.

title: Frankfurt, Germany
text: Frankfurt is a major financial center in Germany on the Main River, home to the European Central Bank. Known for its modern skyline, it hosts a major international airport and important trade fairs.

title: Marseille, France
text: Marseille is a major port city on the Mediterranean coast of southern France. The country's oldest city, it has a diverse culture, a historic old port, and serves as a gateway between Europe and North Africa.

title: Naples, Italy
text: Naples is a historic port city in southern Italy, overlooking a bay with Mount Vesuvius nearby. Regarded as the birthplace of pizza, it lies close to the ancient ruins of Pompeii buried by volcanic eruption.

title: St. Petersburg, Russia
text: St. Petersburg is a major city in Russia on the Baltic Sea, founded by Peter the Great. Known for its canals, palaces, and the vast Hermitage art museum, it served as the imperial capital for two centuries.

title: Kyoto, Japan
text: Kyoto is a city in Japan that served as the imperial capital for over a thousand years. It is renowned for its many classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, and traditional wooden houses.

title: Osaka, Japan
text: Osaka is a large port city in Japan known for its cuisine, lively nightlife, and friendly character. It features Osaka Castle and a modern commercial heart, and serves as a major economic center in western Japan.

title: Guangzhou, China
text: Guangzhou is a major port city in southern China on the Pearl River. A historic trading center once known as Canton, it is a manufacturing and commercial hub with a distinctive Cantonese cuisine and culture.

title: Mecca, Saudi Arabia
text: Mecca is the holiest city in Islam, located in western Saudi Arabia. It is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and the site of the Kaaba, toward which Muslims pray, and the destination of the annual Hajj pilgrimage.

title: Casablanca, Morocco
text: Casablanca is the largest city and economic center of Morocco, on the Atlantic coast. It is known for its blend of Moorish and Art Deco architecture and the towering Hassan II Mosque overlooking the ocean.

title: Lagos, Nigeria
text: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria and one of the biggest in Africa. A coastal megacity and commercial powerhouse, it is known for its bustling markets, music scene, and rapidly growing economy.

title: Johannesburg, South Africa
text: Johannesburg is the largest city in South Africa, grown from a gold-mining settlement on the high inland plateau. It is the country's economic engine and a gateway to the nearby administrative capital, Pretoria.

title: Sao Paulo, Brazil
text: Sao Paulo is the largest city in Brazil and one of the most populous in the world. It is the country's financial and industrial center, known for its vast skyline, cultural diversity, and dynamic food scene.

title: Auckland, New Zealand
text: Auckland is the largest city in New Zealand, built around two harbors on the North Island. Known as the City of Sails for its many boats, it is a diverse, water-oriented city near volcanic cones.

title: Edinburgh, Scotland
text: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland, known for its medieval Old Town and elegant Georgian New Town. It is dominated by Edinburgh Castle on a volcanic crag and hosts a world-famous annual arts festival.

title: Zurich, Switzerland
text: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland, set on a lake at the foot of the Alps. A leading global financial center, it is known for its banking, high quality of life, and well-preserved medieval old town.

title: Geneva, Switzerland
text: Geneva is a city in Switzerland on the shore of Lake Geneva. A center of international diplomacy, it hosts the European headquarters of the United Nations and the International Red Cross, and is famed for watchmaking.

title: Antwerp, Belgium
text: Antwerp is a major port city in Belgium on the Scheldt River. Historically a center of the global diamond trade, it is known for its fashion, art, and the legacy of the painter Peter Paul Rubens.

title: Krakow, Poland
text: Krakow is a historic city in southern Poland that served as the royal capital for centuries. Its well-preserved medieval old town, Wawel Castle, and large market square make it a major cultural destination.

title: Florence, Italy
text: Florence is a city in central Italy regarded as the birthplace of the Renaissance. It is home to masterpieces of art and architecture, including the domed cathedral, the Uffizi Gallery, and Michelangelo's David.

title: Seville, Spain
text: Seville is the capital of the Andalusia region in southern Spain, known for flamenco dancing and Moorish architecture. Its landmarks include the vast Gothic cathedral and the ornate Alcazar royal palace.

title: Marrakech, Morocco
text: Marrakech is a historic city in Morocco at the foot of the Atlas Mountains. Known for its walled medina, bustling souks, and the lively Jemaa el-Fnaa square, it has long been a trading and cultural crossroads.

title: Petra area, Jordan
text: Petra is an ancient city carved into rose-colored sandstone cliffs in southern Jordan. Built by the Nabataeans over two thousand years ago, its elaborate rock-cut facades, including the Treasury, draw visitors from around the world.

title: Chennai, India
text: Chennai is a major city on the southeastern coast of India, on the Bay of Bengal. A cultural center of the Tamil people, it is known for its temples, classical music and dance, long beaches, and film industry.

title: Bangalore, India
text: Bangalore, officially Bengaluru, is a city in southern India known as the country's technology capital. Set on a plateau with a mild climate, it hosts many software and research firms and is nicknamed the Garden City.

title: Kolkata, India
text: Kolkata is a major city in eastern India on the Hooghly River. A former British colonial capital, it is known for its intellectual and artistic heritage, colonial architecture, and vibrant literary tradition.

title: Guadalajara, Mexico
text: Guadalajara is a major city in western Mexico, regarded as the birthplace of mariachi music and tequila. It preserves colonial architecture and is a center of Mexican traditional culture.

title: Cartagena, Colombia
text: Cartagena is a historic port city on Colombia's Caribbean coast. Known for its colorful colonial old town enclosed by stone walls, it was a key Spanish harbor and is now a popular cultural destination.

title: Cusco, Peru
text: Cusco is a city high in the Peruvian Andes that was the capital of the Inca Empire. Its blend of Inca stonework and Spanish colonial buildings makes it a cultural hub and the gateway to Machu Picchu.

title: Valparaiso, Chile
text: Valparaiso is a colorful port city on the coast of Chile, built across steep hills served by funicular lifts. Known for its street art, bohemian culture, and historic harbor, its old quarter is a UNESCO site.

title: Boston, USA
text: Boston is a historic city in the northeastern United States, capital of Massachusetts. One of the oldest cities in the country, it played a central role in the American Revolution and is known for its universities and the Freedom Trail.

title: Seattle, USA
text: Seattle is a major city in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, set between Puget Sound and mountains. Known for its coffee culture, technology industry, and the landmark Space Needle, it is often shrouded in mist.

title: Miami, USA
text: Miami is a coastal city in Florida known for its beaches, Art Deco architecture, and vibrant Latin American culture. A gateway between North and South America, it is a hub for tourism, finance, and cruise travel.

title: New Orleans, USA
text: New Orleans is a city in Louisiana famed for its music, cuisine, and Mardi Gras celebrations. Located near the mouth of the Mississippi River, it blends French, African, and American influences in its distinctive culture.

title: Las Vegas, USA
text: Las Vegas is a city in the Nevada desert known worldwide for its casinos, entertainment, and neon-lit strip of resorts. It has grown from a small railroad town into a major destination for tourism and conventions.

title: Philadelphia, USA
text: Philadelphia is a historic city in the northeastern United States where the Declaration of Independence was signed. Home to the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, it was an early capital of the young nation.

title: Manchester, England
text: Manchester is a major city in northwestern England, a birthplace of the Industrial Revolution. Known for its music scene, football clubs, and role in industrial history, it remains a lively cultural and economic center.

title: Liverpool, England
text: Liverpool is a port city in northwestern England, famous as the home of the Beatles. Its historic waterfront reflects its maritime heritage, and it is known for its music, football, and distinctive local character.

title: Glasgow, Scotland
text: Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland, on the River Clyde. Once a powerhouse of shipbuilding and industry, it is now known for its Victorian architecture, vibrant music scene, and cultural institutions.

title: Lyon, France
text: Lyon is a major city in eastern France, celebrated as a capital of gastronomy. Set where two rivers meet, it preserves a Renaissance old town and has a long history as a center of silk weaving and trade.

title: Nice, France
text: Nice is a city on the French Riviera along the Mediterranean coast. Known for its pebble beaches, the seaside Promenade des Anglais, and its mild climate, it has long attracted artists and holidaymakers.

title: Hamburg, Germany
text: Hamburg is a major port city in northern Germany on the Elbe River. One of Europe's largest ports, it is known for its canals, warehouses, and maritime heritage, with more bridges than many other cities.

title: Cologne, Germany
text: Cologne is a historic city in western Germany on the Rhine River, dominated by its vast Gothic cathedral with twin spires. Founded in Roman times, it is known for its carnival celebrations and its namesake perfume.

title: Turin, Italy
text: Turin is a city in northern Italy at the foot of the Alps, known for its elegant baroque architecture and arcaded streets. A former royal capital, it is a center of the Italian automobile industry.

title: Bologna, Italy
text: Bologna is a city in northern Italy renowned for its cuisine and its ancient university, one of the oldest in the world. It is known for its long porticoed walkways and medieval towers.

title: Valencia, Spain
text: Valencia is a city on the eastern coast of Spain, birthplace of the rice dish paella. It blends a historic old town with the futuristic City of Arts and Sciences complex and lies along the Mediterranean.

title: Bilbao, Spain
text: Bilbao is a city in the Basque Country of northern Spain, transformed by the striking titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum. Once an industrial port, it has become a center of art and modern architecture.

title: Porto, Portugal
text: Porto is a coastal city in northern Portugal, known for its historic riverside district and the port wine that takes its name from the city. Bridges span the Douro River, lined with wine cellars.

title: Rotterdam, Netherlands
text: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands, home to one of the largest ports in Europe. Largely rebuilt after wartime destruction, it is known for its bold modern architecture and cube houses.

title: Gothenburg, Sweden
text: Gothenburg is a major port city on the west coast of Sweden. Known for its canals, seafood, and industrial heritage, it hosts a large university and serves as a hub for shipping and manufacturing.

title: Bergen, Norway
text: Bergen is a coastal city in western Norway surrounded by mountains and fjords. Known for its colorful wooden wharf houses, a legacy of the Hanseatic trade, it is often called the gateway to the fjords.

title: Gdansk, Poland
text: Gdansk is a historic port city on the Baltic coast of Poland. Known for its richly decorated old town and long maritime history, it was the birthplace of the Solidarity movement.

title: Thessaloniki, Greece
text: Thessaloniki is the second-largest city in Greece, a port on the Aegean Sea. Rich in Byzantine and Ottoman heritage, it is known for its waterfront, White Tower, and vibrant cultural life.

title: Yokohama, Japan
text: Yokohama is a major port city in Japan, just south of Tokyo. One of the first Japanese ports opened to foreign trade, it is known for its harbor, waterfront district, and large Chinatown.

title: Sapporo, Japan
text: Sapporo is the largest city on the northern Japanese island of Hokkaido. Known for its cold, snowy winters, an annual snow festival, and its namesake beer, it hosted the Winter Olympics in 1972.

title: Busan, South Korea
text: Busan is a major port city in South Korea, set on the southeastern coast. Known for its beaches, seafood markets, and mountain temples, it hosts a prominent international film festival.

title: Shenzhen, China
text: Shenzhen is a major city in southern China near Hong Kong, transformed from a fishing village into a technology and manufacturing powerhouse. It is a symbol of China's rapid modernization and economic growth.

title: Chengdu, China
text: Chengdu is a major city in southwestern China, capital of Sichuan province. Known for its spicy cuisine and relaxed teahouse culture, it is home to a famous research base for the conservation of giant pandas.

title: Xi'an, China
text: Xi'an is a historic city in central China that served as the capital of several ancient dynasties. It marked the eastern end of the Silk Road and is famous for the nearby Terracotta Army.

title: Delhi metropolitan area, India
text: Delhi is a vast metropolitan area in northern India that contains the capital, New Delhi. A city of many layers of history, it holds Mughal monuments such as the Red Fort and Humayun's Tomb alongside modern districts.

title: Hyderabad, India
text: Hyderabad is a major city in southern India, historically ruled by nizams and known for its distinctive cuisine and the Charminar monument. Today it is a leading center of the information technology industry.

title: Karachi, Pakistan
text: Karachi is the largest city and main port of Pakistan, on the Arabian Sea. A bustling commercial and financial center, it is one of the most populous cities in the world and a hub of the country's economy.

title: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
text: Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, is the largest city in Vietnam. A dynamic commercial center, it blends French colonial buildings, bustling markets, and a fast-paced modern energy.

title: Bali, Indonesia
text: Bali is an Indonesian island famous for its beaches, rice terraces, and Hindu temples. A major tourist destination, it is known for its distinctive culture, art, and spiritual traditions that set it apart from the rest of the country.

title: Chiang Mai, Thailand
text: Chiang Mai is a city in the mountains of northern Thailand, known for its many Buddhist temples and its old walled center. A center of Lanna culture, it is popular for crafts, cuisine, and nearby hill villages.

title: Alexandria, Egypt
text: Alexandria is a major port city on Egypt's Mediterranean coast, founded by Alexander the Great. Once home to a legendary ancient library and lighthouse, it remains an important cultural and commercial center.

title: Fez, Morocco
text: Fez is a historic city in Morocco, home to one of the world's oldest universities and a vast walled medina. Its maze of narrow streets, traditional crafts, and leather tanneries preserve a medieval character.

title: Zanzibar, Tanzania
text: Zanzibar is an island off the coast of Tanzania in the Indian Ocean, known for its spice trade and beaches. Its historic Stone Town, a blend of African, Arab, and European influences, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Timbuktu, Mali
text: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali on the edge of the Sahara. Once a fabled center of trade and Islamic scholarship, it is known for its ancient mud-brick mosques and manuscripts.

title: Salvador, Brazil
text: Salvador is a coastal city in northeastern Brazil, once the country's colonial capital. Known for its Afro-Brazilian culture, colorful historic center, and vibrant music and cuisine, it lies on the Atlantic coast.

title: Medellin, Colombia
text: Medellin is a city in Colombia set in a valley in the Andes, known for its spring-like climate year-round. Once notorious for violence, it has transformed into a hub of innovation, culture, and urban renewal.

title: Quebec City, Canada
text: Quebec City is a historic city in eastern Canada, the capital of the province of Quebec. Its fortified old town, the only walled city north of Mexico, preserves a strong French heritage and colonial architecture.

title: Montreal, Canada
text: Montreal is a major city in the Canadian province of Quebec, the largest French-speaking city in the Americas after Paris. It is known for its festivals, cuisine, and blend of European charm and North American energy.

title: Monterrey, Mexico
text: Monterrey is a major industrial city in northeastern Mexico, set among rugged mountains. A center of business and manufacturing, it is one of the country's wealthiest and most modern urban centers.

title: Perth, Australia
text: Perth is the capital of Western Australia and one of the most isolated major cities in the world. Set on the Swan River near the Indian Ocean, it is known for its sunny climate, beaches, and parks.

title: Brisbane, Australia
text: Brisbane is a major city in eastern Australia, capital of Queensland, set on the Brisbane River. Known for its warm climate, riverside parklands, and proximity to beaches and rainforests, it is a growing urban center.

title: Adelaide, Australia
text: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, a planned city known for its parklands, festivals, and nearby wine regions. Set on a coastal plain, it has a relaxed character and a strong arts culture.

title: Denver, USA
text: Denver is the capital of Colorado, USA, known as the Mile-High City for sitting about a mile above sea level. Set at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, it is a gateway to skiing and outdoor recreation in the American West.

title: Atlanta, USA
text: Atlanta is a major city in the southeastern United States, capital of Georgia. A transportation and business hub with one of the world's busiest airports, it played a central role in the American civil rights movement.

title: Houston, USA
text: Houston is a large city in Texas, USA, and a center of the American energy and space industries. It is home to a major NASA control center and is known for its diverse population and sprawling metropolitan area.

title: San Diego, USA
text: San Diego is a coastal city in Southern California near the Mexican border. Known for its mild climate, beaches, and large natural harbor, it is home to a famous zoo and a significant naval presence.

title: Portland, USA
text: Portland is a city in Oregon in the Pacific Northwest of the United States. Known for its parks, bridges over the Willamette River, coffee and craft beer culture, and an emphasis on the environment and cycling.

title: Nagoya, Japan
text: Nagoya is a major industrial city in central Japan, a center of the country's automobile manufacturing. It is home to a historic castle and lies along the Pacific coast between Tokyo and Osaka.

title: Fukuoka, Japan
text: Fukuoka is a major port city on the Japanese island of Kyushu, closer to mainland Asia than to Tokyo. Known for its food stalls, festivals, and coastal setting, it is a growing regional business center.

title: Chongqing, China
text: Chongqing is a vast, hilly municipality in southwestern China set where two rivers meet. A major inland port on the Yangtze, it is known for its spicy hotpot cuisine and dramatic, multilevel urban landscape.

title: Wuhan, China
text: Wuhan is a major city in central China on the Yangtze River, formed from three historic towns. A key transportation and industrial hub, it is known for its bridges, universities, and role in Chinese history.

title: Tianjin, China
text: Tianjin is a large port city in northern China near Beijing. A historic center of trade with distinctive foreign-influenced districts, it serves as a major gateway to the capital by sea.

title: Kobe, Japan
text: Kobe is a port city in Japan set between mountains and the sea. Known for its scenic harbor, cosmopolitan history as an early open port, and its famous premium beef, it is a hub of western Japan.

title: Pune, India
text: Pune is a major city in western India, historically a center of Marathi culture. Today it is known for its universities, information technology industry, and pleasant climate in the hills near Mumbai.

title: Ahmedabad, India
text: Ahmedabad is a large city in western India in the state of Gujarat. Known for its textile industry, historic old city, and association with Mahatma Gandhi, whose ashram there is a place of pilgrimage.

title: Jaipur, India
text: Jaipur is a historic city in northwestern India known as the Pink City for the color of its old buildings. The capital of Rajasthan, it is famous for its palaces, forts, and the astronomical instruments of the Jantar Mantar.

title: Lahore, Pakistan
text: Lahore is a major city in eastern Pakistan, considered the country's cultural heart. Rich in Mughal heritage, it is home to the grand Badshahi Mosque, the Lahore Fort, and lively gardens and bazaars.

title: Chittagong, Bangladesh
text: Chittagong is the main seaport of Bangladesh, on the coast near the Bay of Bengal. A busy commercial and industrial center, it is surrounded by hills and lies along important shipping routes.

title: Surabaya, Indonesia
text: Surabaya is the second-largest city in Indonesia, a major port on the island of Java. A center of trade and industry, it played an important role in the country's struggle for independence.

title: Cebu, Philippines
text: Cebu is a major city and port in the central Philippines, one of the country's oldest. A commercial and cultural hub of the region, it is known for its historic sites and as a gateway to nearby island beaches.

title: Da Nang, Vietnam
text: Da Nang is a coastal city in central Vietnam, known for its beaches and as a gateway to the historic towns of Hoi An and Hue. It has grown into a major port and a popular seaside destination.

title: Phuket, Thailand
text: Phuket is Thailand's largest island, a popular resort destination in the Andaman Sea. Known for its beaches, clear waters, and nightlife, it draws visitors from around the world to its tropical shores.

title: Aleppo, Syria
text: Aleppo is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, in northern Syria. Historically a great trading city along caravan routes, it is known for its ancient citadel and covered markets.

title: Isfahan, Iran
text: Isfahan is a historic city in central Iran renowned for its stunning Islamic architecture. Its vast central square, blue-tiled mosques, and arched bridges made it a jewel of Persian art and a former capital.

title: Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
text: Jeddah is a major port city on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia. A commercial hub and the main gateway for pilgrims traveling to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, it blends historic and modern districts.

title: Medina, Saudi Arabia
text: Medina is a holy city in western Saudi Arabia, the second-holiest in Islam after Mecca. It is where the Prophet Muhammad is buried, and its central mosque is a major destination for Muslim pilgrims.

title: Tel Aviv, Israel
text: Tel Aviv is a modern coastal city in Israel on the Mediterranean, known for its beaches, nightlife, and technology industry. It contains a notable collection of Bauhaus architecture in its White City district.

title: Sharjah, UAE
text: Sharjah is one of the emirates of the United Arab Emirates, adjoining Dubai. Known as a center of Islamic culture and the arts, it houses museums and heritage sites and takes a more conservative character than its neighbor.

title: Durban, South Africa
text: Durban is a major port city on the east coast of South Africa on the Indian Ocean. Known for its warm climate, beaches, and large Indian community, it is a popular holiday destination and busy harbor.

title: Mombasa, Kenya
text: Mombasa is a historic port city on the coast of Kenya, its second-largest city. A center of trade for centuries, it blends Swahili, Arab, Indian, and European influences and lies along the Indian Ocean.

title: Abidjan, Ivory Coast
text: Abidjan is the largest city and economic capital of Ivory Coast, a bustling port on the Gulf of Guinea. Known for its modern skyline and lagoons, it is one of the major urban centers of West Africa.

title: Kano, Nigeria
text: Kano is a historic city in northern Nigeria, long a center of trade across the Sahara. One of the oldest cities in West Africa, it is known for its ancient walls, dye pits, and role in the region's commerce.

title: Djenne, Mali
text: Djenne is a historic town in Mali, once a great center of trade and Islamic learning along Saharan routes. It is famous for its Great Mosque, the largest mud-brick building in the world, rebuilt by the community each year.

title: Recife, Brazil
text: Recife is a major coastal city in northeastern Brazil, sometimes called the Venice of Brazil for its rivers and bridges. A historic port, it is known for its beaches, carnival, and colonial architecture.

title: Curitiba, Brazil
text: Curitiba is a city in southern Brazil widely recognized for its innovative urban planning and public transport. Known for extensive parks and environmental initiatives, it is often cited as a model green city.

title: Rosario, Argentina
text: Rosario is a major city in Argentina on the Parana River, an important port and industrial center. Known for its grand architecture and riverside setting, it is one of the country's largest cities.

title: Guayaquil, Ecuador
text: Guayaquil is the largest city and main port of Ecuador, on the Pacific coast. A commercial and industrial hub, it serves as a gateway to the country and to the Galapagos Islands.

title: Arequipa, Peru
text: Arequipa is a city in southern Peru set beneath volcanoes, known as the White City for its buildings of pale volcanic stone. Its historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site framed by dramatic peaks.

title: Puebla, Mexico
text: Puebla is a historic city in central Mexico known for its colonial architecture and colorful Talavera tiles. It is famed for its cuisine, including the rich sauce mole poblano, and lies near snow-capped volcanoes.

title: Oaxaca, Mexico
text: Oaxaca is a city in southern Mexico celebrated for its Indigenous cultures, crafts, and cuisine. Its well-preserved colonial center and nearby ancient ruins make it a rich cultural destination.

title: Christchurch, New Zealand
text: Christchurch is the largest city on New Zealand's South Island, known as the Garden City for its parks and the River Avon. Rebuilt after major earthquakes, it serves as a gateway to the Southern Alps.

title: Gold Coast, Australia
text: The Gold Coast is a coastal city in eastern Australia known for its long sandy beaches, surf, and high-rise skyline. A major tourist destination, it lies south of Brisbane along the Pacific Ocean.

title: Cairns, Australia
text: Cairns is a city in tropical northern Australia, a popular gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and nearby rainforests. Its warm climate and marine access make it a hub for reef and nature tourism.

title: Antalya, Turkey
text: Antalya is a resort city on the Mediterranean coast of Turkey, known for its beaches, ancient ruins, and old harbor. A major tourist destination, it lies along a scenic stretch of coastline backed by mountains.

title: Dubrovnik, Croatia
text: Dubrovnik is a historic walled city on the Adriatic coast of Croatia, often called the Pearl of the Adriatic. Its well-preserved stone ramparts, red-roofed old town, and harbor make it a renowned destination.

title: Salzburg, Austria
text: Salzburg is a city in Austria near the German border, the birthplace of the composer Mozart. Set against alpine scenery, its baroque old town and hilltop fortress make it one of the country's most visited places.

title: Bruges, Belgium
text: Bruges is a well-preserved medieval city in Belgium, famed for its canals, cobbled streets, and market square. Sometimes called the Venice of the North, its historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across northern China over many centuries to guard against invasions. Winding for thousands of kilometres over mountains and deserts, it is one of the most famous structures ever built by human hands.

title: Pyramids of Giza
text: The Pyramids of Giza in Egypt are ancient royal tombs built over 4,500 years ago near Cairo. The Great Pyramid is the oldest and only largely surviving structure among the classical Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and the Great Sphinx guards the complex.

title: Colosseum
text: The Colosseum is a vast ancient amphitheater in the center of Rome, Italy. Built in the first century, it once held tens of thousands of spectators for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles, and remains an iconic symbol of the Roman Empire.

title: Taj Mahal
text: The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum in Agra, India, built in the 17th century by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife. Renowned for its symmetry and inlaid stonework, it is celebrated as a masterpiece of Islamic architecture and a monument to love.

title: Machu Picchu
text: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel set high in the Andes of Peru. Built of precisely fitted stone and abandoned within a century, it was largely unknown to the outside world until 1911 and is now a renowned archaeological site.

title: Petra
text: Petra is an ancient city in southern Jordan, famous for its temples and tombs carved directly into rose-colored rock. Established by the Nabataeans, it flourished as a trading hub and its ornate Treasury facade is among the most photographed monuments in the world.

title: Eiffel Tower
text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower in Paris, France, built for the 1889 World's Fair. Designed by Gustave Eiffel, it stands over 300 metres tall and has become the enduring symbol of Paris and one of the most visited monuments on Earth.

title: Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal copper statue on an island in New York Harbor, a gift from France to the United States dedicated in 1886. Depicting a robed figure holding a torch, it has long symbolized freedom and welcome to immigrants.

title: Christ the Redeemer
text: Christ the Redeemer is a giant statue of Jesus atop Corcovado mountain overlooking Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Completed in 1931, the Art Deco figure stands with outstretched arms and is a symbol of the city and of Christianity worldwide.

title: Sydney Opera House
text: The Sydney Opera House is a performing arts center on the harbor of Sydney, Australia. Its distinctive shell-shaped roofs, completed in 1973, make it one of the most recognizable buildings of the 20th century and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Big Ben
text: Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell of the clock tower at the Houses of Parliament in London, though it commonly refers to the tower itself. A symbol of the United Kingdom, the clock has kept time above the Thames since the 1850s.

title: Leaning Tower of Pisa
text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is a freestanding bell tower in Pisa, Italy, famous for its unintended tilt caused by soft, unstable ground. Begun in the 12th century, it leans noticeably to one side and has become one of Italy's most beloved landmarks.

title: Angkor Wat
text: Angkor Wat is a vast temple complex in Cambodia, built in the 12th century and originally dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu. The largest religious monument in the world, its towers appear on the Cambodian national flag.

title: Stonehenge
text: Stonehenge is a prehistoric monument in southern England consisting of a ring of massive standing stones. Erected thousands of years ago, its exact purpose remains debated, and it is aligned with the movements of the sun at the solstices.

title: Acropolis of Athens
text: The Acropolis is an ancient citadel on a rocky hill above Athens, Greece. It is crowned by the Parthenon, a temple to the goddess Athena built in the 5th century BC, and stands as a symbol of classical Greek civilization and democracy.

title: Sagrada Familia
text: The Sagrada Familia is a large basilica in Barcelona, Spain, designed by the architect Antoni Gaudi. Begun in 1882 and still under construction, its soaring, organic towers make it one of the most distinctive churches in the world.

title: Golden Gate Bridge
text: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the entrance to San Francisco Bay in California. Completed in 1937 and painted a distinctive orange-red, it is celebrated as a triumph of engineering and a symbol of the American West Coast.

title: Mount Rushmore
text: Mount Rushmore is a monumental sculpture carved into a granite mountainside in South Dakota, USA. It depicts the faces of four American presidents, Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln, each about 18 metres high.

title: Burj Khalifa
text: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is the tallest building in the world, rising more than 800 metres. Completed in 2010, its tapering spire dominates the city skyline and offers observation decks with sweeping desert and sea views.

title: Chichen Itza
text: Chichen Itza is a large ancient Maya city in Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula. Its centerpiece is the stepped pyramid known as El Castillo, whose design reflects the Maya calendar and casts a serpent-shaped shadow at the equinoxes.

title: Great Sphinx
text: The Great Sphinx of Giza is a colossal limestone statue in Egypt with the body of a lion and the head of a human. Carved over 4,500 years ago near the pyramids, it is one of the largest and oldest monumental sculptures in the world.

title: Neuschwanstein Castle
text: Neuschwanstein is a fairytale hilltop castle in Bavaria, Germany, built in the 19th century for King Ludwig II. Its romantic towers inspired later fantasy castles and it stands dramatically against a backdrop of forested Alpine foothills.

title: Moai of Easter Island
text: The Moai are monumental stone statues on Easter Island in the Pacific Ocean, carved by the Rapa Nui people centuries ago. Nearly a thousand of these massive human figures dot the remote island, and their creation and transport remain subjects of study.

title: Terracotta Army
text: The Terracotta Army is a collection of thousands of life-sized clay soldiers buried near Xi'an, China, to guard the tomb of the first emperor. Created over two thousand years ago and rediscovered in 1974, each figure has individually crafted features.

title: Hagia Sophia
text: The Hagia Sophia in Istanbul, Turkey, is a monumental domed building that has served as a cathedral, a mosque, and a museum over its long history. Built in the 6th century, it was a marvel of Byzantine engineering and remains an architectural landmark.

title: Alhambra
text: The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain, built by Moorish rulers. Renowned for its intricate Islamic decoration, courtyards, and fountains, it is one of the finest examples of Moorish architecture in the world.

title: Mont-Saint-Michel
text: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island in Normandy, France, crowned by a medieval abbey. Surrounded by vast sand flats and dramatic tides, the rocky islet and its spire have drawn pilgrims and visitors for over a thousand years.

title: Brandenburg Gate
text: The Brandenburg Gate is a neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany, built in the 18th century. Once a symbol of a divided city during the Cold War, it now stands as a symbol of German reunification and European unity.

title: Tower Bridge
text: Tower Bridge is a combined bascule and suspension bridge over the River Thames in London. Completed in 1894 with its distinctive twin towers, its central span can be raised to allow tall ships to pass, and it is often confused with London Bridge.

title: Notre-Dame Cathedral
text: Notre-Dame de Paris is a medieval Gothic cathedral on an island in the Seine in Paris, France. Famous for its flying buttresses, rose windows, and gargoyles, it took nearly two centuries to build and remains a masterpiece of Gothic architecture.

title: St. Basil's Cathedral
text: St. Basil's Cathedral stands on Red Square in Moscow, Russia, famed for its brightly colored, swirling onion domes. Built in the 16th century, its whimsical silhouette has become one of the most recognizable symbols of Russia.

title: Forbidden City
text: The Forbidden City is a vast palace complex in the heart of Beijing, China, that served as the imperial residence for centuries. With hundreds of buildings behind red walls, it is one of the largest and best-preserved ancient palace complexes in the world.

title: Times Square
text: Times Square is a bustling commercial intersection in Manhattan, New York City, famed for its dazzling illuminated billboards and theaters. Often called the Crossroads of the World, it hosts a celebrated New Year's Eve ball drop each year.

title: Empire State Building
text: The Empire State Building is an Art Deco skyscraper in New York City completed in 1931. For decades the tallest building in the world, its distinctive silhouette and observation decks remain among the most iconic in the American skyline.

title: Great Barrier Reef landmark
text: The Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the largest coral reef system in the world, stretching over 2,000 kilometres. Visible from space, it hosts an extraordinary diversity of marine life and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Uluru
text: Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock, is a massive sandstone monolith in the arid heart of Australia. Sacred to the Indigenous Anangu people, it glows red at sunrise and sunset and rises dramatically from the surrounding desert plain.

title: Victoria Falls landmark
text: Victoria Falls, on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe, is one of the largest waterfalls in the world. Known locally as the Smoke that Thunders for its towering spray, its curtain of water plunges into a deep gorge.

title: Niagara Falls
text: Niagara Falls is a group of three powerful waterfalls on the border between Canada and the United States. Renowned for their volume of flowing water and mist, they are a major tourist destination and a source of hydroelectric power.

title: Grand Canyon landmark
text: The Grand Canyon in Arizona, USA, is a vast gorge carved by the Colorado River over millions of years. Reaching over a mile deep, its layered red rock walls reveal billions of years of geological history and draw visitors from around the world.

title: Panama Canal landmark
text: The Panama Canal is an artificial waterway across the Isthmus of Panama linking the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Opened in 1914, its system of locks lifts ships over the land, dramatically shortening voyages between the two oceans.

title: Golden Temple
text: The Golden Temple, or Harmandir Sahib, in Amritsar, India, is the holiest shrine of Sikhism. Covered in gold and set amid a sacred pool, it welcomes visitors of all faiths and serves free communal meals to hundreds of thousands each day.

title: Borobudur
text: Borobudur, on the island of Java in Indonesia, is the largest Buddhist temple in the world. Built in the 9th century, its terraces of stone reliefs and bell-shaped stupas form a mandala that pilgrims ascend as a spiritual journey.

title: Wailing Wall
text: The Western Wall, also called the Wailing Wall, in Jerusalem is a remnant of the ancient Second Temple's retaining structure. It is the holiest place where Jews are permitted to pray, and visitors often place written prayers between its stones.

title: Sistine Chapel
text: The Sistine Chapel in Vatican City is renowned for its ceiling painted by Michelangelo in the early 16th century, including the famous Creation of Adam. It is where the College of Cardinals gathers to elect a new pope.

title: Kremlin
text: The Kremlin is a fortified complex in the center of Moscow, Russia, that serves as the seat of the Russian government. Enclosed by red walls, it contains palaces, cathedrals, and towers and overlooks Red Square.

title: Pyramid of the Sun
text: The Pyramid of the Sun is a massive ancient structure at Teotihuacan near Mexico City. One of the largest pyramids in the Americas, it was built by a civilization that flourished centuries before the Aztecs, who later named the abandoned city.

title: Louvre Museum
text: The Louvre in Paris is one of the largest and most visited art museums in the world. Housed in a former royal palace and marked by a glass pyramid entrance, it holds masterpieces including Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa.

title: Buckingham Palace
text: Buckingham Palace in London is the official residence of the British monarch. Known for its ceremonial Changing of the Guard, its balcony appearances, and its grand facade, it is a focal point of national events in the United Kingdom.

title: Vatican and St. Peter's
text: St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City is one of the largest churches in the world and a center of the Roman Catholic Church. Built over the traditional burial site of Saint Peter, it features a vast dome designed by Michelangelo.

title: Pompeii
text: Pompeii is an ancient Roman city near Naples, Italy, buried under ash by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79. Remarkably preserved, its excavated streets, houses, and frescoes offer a vivid glimpse into daily Roman life.

title: The Parthenon
text: The Parthenon is an ancient temple on the Acropolis of Athens, dedicated to the goddess Athena. Built in the 5th century BC, its elegant columns and proportions make it a defining monument of classical Greek architecture.

title: Palace of Versailles
text: The Palace of Versailles near Paris was the principal royal residence of France before the Revolution. Famed for its opulent Hall of Mirrors and vast formal gardens, it symbolizes the power of the French monarchy.

title: Windsor Castle
text: Windsor Castle, west of London, is the oldest and largest inhabited castle in the world and a residence of the British royal family. It has served monarchs for nearly a thousand years and blends fortress and palace.

title: Edinburgh Castle
text: Edinburgh Castle sits atop a volcanic rock overlooking the Scottish capital. A historic fortress and former royal residence, it houses the Scottish crown jewels and fires a ceremonial gun each day.

title: Sydney Harbour Bridge
text: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel arch bridge spanning the harbor of Sydney, Australia. Completed in 1932 and nicknamed the Coathanger, it carries road, rail, and pedestrian traffic and offers climbs to its summit.

title: CN Tower
text: The CN Tower in Toronto, Canada, is a tall telecommunications and observation tower that was among the tallest freestanding structures in the world when completed in 1976. It offers panoramic views and a glass floor high above the city.

title: Space Needle
text: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle, USA, built for the 1962 World's Fair. Its distinctive saucer-shaped top has become an enduring symbol of the city and offers sweeping views of the surrounding region.

title: Gateway Arch
text: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, USA, is a sweeping stainless-steel arch commemorating the westward expansion of the United States. Rising over 190 metres, it is the tallest arch in the world and carries visitors to an observation deck.

title: Merlion of Singapore
text: The Merlion is a statue with the head of a lion and the body of a fish that serves as a national symbol of Singapore. Spouting water into Marina Bay, it represents the city's origins as a fishing village and its lion-city name.

title: Petronas Towers
text: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, are twin skyscrapers linked by a sky bridge. Completed in 1998, they were briefly the tallest buildings in the world and remain a striking symbol of modern Malaysia.

title: Marina Bay Sands
text: Marina Bay Sands in Singapore is a landmark resort crowned by a boat-shaped structure spanning three towers. Its rooftop infinity pool and sky park have become an icon of the city's futuristic skyline.

title: Shwedagon Pagoda
text: The Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, Myanmar, is a gilded Buddhist stupa said to enshrine relics of the Buddha. Covered in gold and topped with jewels, it is the most sacred Buddhist site in the country.

title: Wat Arun
text: Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, stands on the banks of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok, Thailand. Its central spire, decorated with colorful porcelain, catches the light beautifully and is a symbol of the city.

title: Potala Palace
text: The Potala Palace in Lhasa, Tibet, was the traditional residence of the Dalai Lama. Rising in tiers up a hillside, this vast white-and-red fortress-monastery is a masterpiece of Tibetan architecture and a UNESCO site.

title: Registan Samarkand
text: The Registan is the majestic central square of Samarkand, Uzbekistan, framed by three grand tiled madrasas. A jewel of Islamic architecture along the Silk Road, it dazzles with turquoise domes and intricate mosaics.

title: Blue Mosque
text: The Blue Mosque, or Sultan Ahmed Mosque, in Istanbul, Turkey, is famed for the blue tiles that decorate its interior. Built in the early 17th century, its cascade of domes and six minarets make it an architectural landmark.

title: Dome of the Rock
text: The Dome of the Rock is a shrine with a golden dome on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. An early masterpiece of Islamic architecture, it is one of the most recognizable landmarks in the holy city.

title: Abu Simbel
text: Abu Simbel comprises two massive rock temples in southern Egypt, built by the pharaoh Ramesses II. In the 20th century the entire complex was moved to higher ground to save it from flooding by the Aswan Dam reservoir.

title: Valley of the Kings
text: The Valley of the Kings near Luxor, Egypt, is a burial ground where many pharaohs, including Tutankhamun, were entombed. Its rock-cut tombs, decorated with vivid paintings, have revealed treasures of ancient Egypt.

title: Karnak Temple
text: The Karnak Temple complex near Luxor, Egypt, is one of the largest religious sites ever built. Its vast hall of towering stone columns and rows of sphinxes reflect the grandeur of ancient Egyptian temple architecture.

title: Great Zimbabwe
text: Great Zimbabwe is a ruined ancient city in southern Africa built of dry-stone walls without mortar. Once the center of a powerful medieval kingdom, its stone enclosures gave the modern nation of Zimbabwe its name.

title: Timgad
text: Timgad is a remarkably preserved Roman city in the Algerian desert, laid out on a precise grid. Founded as a colony for army veterans, its arches, theater, and streets illustrate Roman town planning in North Africa.

title: Tikal
text: Tikal is a major ancient Maya city in the rainforest of Guatemala. Its towering stone pyramids rise above the jungle canopy, and it was one of the most powerful kingdoms of the classic Maya civilization.

title: Nazca Lines
text: The Nazca Lines are enormous ancient designs etched into the desert of southern Peru, depicting animals, plants, and shapes. Best seen from the air, they were created by the Nazca culture and their exact purpose remains debated.

title: Salar de Uyuni
text: The Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the largest salt flat in the world, a vast white expanse high in the Andes. During the rainy season a thin layer of water turns it into a giant mirror reflecting the sky.

title: Iguazu landmark
text: The Devil's Throat is the most dramatic part of Iguazu Falls on the Argentina-Brazil border, a horseshoe of thundering cascades. Surrounding rainforest and rainbows in the spray make it one of South America's greatest natural sights.

title: Perito Moreno Glacier
text: The Perito Moreno Glacier in Argentine Patagonia is a vast, advancing river of ice. Visitors can watch huge chunks calve from its towering front into the lake below, making it one of the most accessible great glaciers.

title: Torres del Paine
text: Torres del Paine is a national park in Chilean Patagonia famed for its dramatic granite towers, turquoise lakes, and glaciers. It is a premier destination for hiking amid some of the most striking mountain scenery on Earth.

title: Yellowstone
text: Yellowstone in the United States was the world's first national park. It is known for its geysers, including Old Faithful, colorful hot springs, and abundant wildlife such as bison, wolves, and bears atop a giant volcanic system.

title: Yosemite
text: Yosemite National Park in California, USA, is renowned for its sheer granite cliffs, giant sequoia trees, and waterfalls. Landmarks such as El Capitan and Half Dome draw climbers and nature lovers from around the world.

title: Banff National Park
text: Banff National Park in the Canadian Rockies is the country's oldest national park. Known for its turquoise glacial lakes, snow-capped peaks, and abundant wildlife, it is a centerpiece of Canada's mountain wilderness.

title: Grand Canyon park
text: Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona protects one of the most spectacular gorges on Earth, carved by the Colorado River. Its immense scale and layered red rock walls attract millions of visitors every year.

title: Milford Sound
text: Milford Sound is a stunning fjord in the Fiordland region of New Zealand's South Island. Framed by sheer cliffs, waterfalls, and rainforest, it is one of the country's most celebrated natural attractions.

title: Ha Long Bay
text: Ha Long Bay in northern Vietnam is famed for its thousands of limestone islands and pillars rising from emerald waters. A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is often explored by boat among its caves and hidden coves.

title: Guilin landscape
text: The karst mountains around Guilin and the Li River in southern China form a landscape of dramatic limestone peaks. Their misty, sculptural forms have inspired Chinese painters and poets for centuries.

title: Plitvice Lakes
text: Plitvice Lakes National Park in Croatia is famous for a chain of terraced lakes joined by waterfalls, set amid forest. Its vivid turquoise waters and wooden walkways make it one of Europe's most beautiful natural parks.

title: Cliffs of Moher
text: The Cliffs of Moher on the western coast of Ireland rise sharply from the Atlantic Ocean. Stretching for several kilometres and home to seabird colonies, they are among Ireland's most visited natural landmarks.

title: Giant's Causeway
text: The Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland is a coastal formation of thousands of interlocking basalt columns created by ancient volcanic activity. Its geometric stone steps are steeped in local legend.

title: Santorini
text: Santorini is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea, famed for whitewashed villages perched on cliffs above a flooded volcanic caldera. Its blue-domed churches and sunset views make it one of the Mediterranean's most iconic destinations.

title: Meteora
text: Meteora in central Greece is a cluster of monasteries built atop towering natural rock pillars. Perched dramatically above the plain, these Orthodox retreats are a remarkable blend of faith and precarious location.

title: Alhambra gardens
text: The Generalife gardens beside the Alhambra in Granada, Spain, were the summer retreat of Moorish rulers. With fountains, pools, and terraced greenery, they exemplify the Islamic ideal of a garden as an earthly paradise.

title: Nile River
text: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing northward through northeastern Africa to the Mediterranean Sea. It has two main tributaries, the White Nile and the Blue Nile, and its waters have sustained Egyptian civilization for thousands of years.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon in South America is the largest river in the world by volume of water, carrying more than any other. Rising in the Andes and flowing across Brazil to the Atlantic, it drains the vast Amazon rainforest, the largest on Earth.

title: Yangtze River
text: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, flowing across China from the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea near Shanghai. A vital artery for transport and agriculture, it is spanned by the enormous Three Gorges Dam.

title: Mississippi River
text: The Mississippi is a major river of North America, flowing southward through the central United States to the Gulf of Mexico. With its tributary the Missouri, it forms one of the largest river systems on the continent.

title: Yellow River
text: The Yellow River, or Huang He, is a major river in northern China, often called the cradle of Chinese civilization. It carries large amounts of yellow silt that give it its name and has historically been prone to devastating floods.

title: Danube River
text: The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe, flowing from Germany's Black Forest eastward through several countries to the Black Sea. It passes through capitals including Vienna, Budapest, and Belgrade.

title: Ganges River
text: The Ganges is a major river of South Asia, flowing from the Himalayas across northern India and Bangladesh to the Bay of Bengal. Sacred to Hindus, its banks host holy cities such as Varanasi, and it supports hundreds of millions of people.

title: Volga River
text: The Volga is the longest river in Europe, flowing through western Russia to the Caspian Sea. A central waterway of Russian history and commerce, it is linked by canals to other seas and is dotted with major cities.

title: Congo River
text: The Congo is a great river of Central Africa and one of the deepest in the world. It flows in a broad arc through dense rainforest, crossing the equator twice, before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Mekong River
text: The Mekong is a major river of Southeast Asia, flowing from the Tibetan Plateau through China, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam to the South China Sea. Its rich delta supports intensive rice farming and dense populations.

title: Rhine River
text: The Rhine is one of the major rivers of Europe, flowing from the Swiss Alps through Germany and the Netherlands to the North Sea. An important trade route since ancient times, its valley is lined with castles and vineyards.

title: Colorado River
text: The Colorado River flows through the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. Over millions of years it carved the Grand Canyon, and today its waters are heavily used for irrigation and drinking supply across arid regions.

title: Indus River
text: The Indus is a major river of South Asia, flowing from the Tibetan Plateau through India and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. It gave its name to India and supported one of the world's earliest urban civilizations.

title: Zambezi River
text: The Zambezi is a major river in southern Africa, flowing east to the Indian Ocean. It is best known for Victoria Falls, one of the world's largest waterfalls, which lies on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

title: Seine River
text: The Seine is a river in northern France that flows through Paris on its way to the English Channel. Its banks in the capital are lined with famous monuments, and it has long inspired artists and writers.

title: Thames River
text: The Thames is the principal river of England, flowing through London to the North Sea. Its banks host landmarks such as the Houses of Parliament, Tower Bridge, and the London Eye, and it has been central to the city's history.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China in the Himalayas, is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level, reaching about 8,849 metres. It draws mountaineers from around the world, though its extreme altitude makes climbing perilous.

title: K2
text: K2, in the Karakoram range on the border of Pakistan and China, is the second-highest mountain on Earth. Steeper and more technically difficult than Everest, it has earned a reputation as one of the deadliest peaks to climb.

title: Himalayas
text: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world, stretching across Asia through several countries. They contain the tallest peaks on Earth, including Everest, and are the source of major rivers such as the Ganges and Indus.

title: Andes
text: The Andes are the longest continental mountain range in the world, running down the western edge of South America. They contain high plateaus, active volcanoes, and Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia.

title: Alps
text: The Alps are a major mountain range in Europe, curving through several countries including France, Switzerland, Italy, and Austria. Known for peaks such as the Matterhorn and Mont Blanc, they are a center for skiing and mountaineering.

title: Rocky Mountains
text: The Rocky Mountains stretch through western North America from Canada into the United States. Known for their rugged peaks, national parks, and the Continental Divide, they form a spine along the western part of the continent.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro
text: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa, rising about 5,895 metres. A dormant volcano standing alone above the surrounding plains, its summit has long carried glaciers despite lying near the equator.

title: Mont Blanc
text: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps and Western Europe, rising on the border between France and Italy. Its snow-covered summit and glaciers make it a landmark of mountaineering and a popular destination near Chamonix.

title: Matterhorn
text: The Matterhorn is a distinctive pyramid-shaped peak in the Alps on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Its steep, near-symmetrical faces make it one of the most recognizable and photographed mountains in the world.

title: Mount Fuji
text: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan and an active volcano with a near-perfect symmetrical cone. Sacred in Japanese culture and a frequent subject of art, it is a popular climbing destination during the summer season.

title: Aconcagua
text: Aconcagua, in the Andes of western Argentina, is the highest mountain outside of Asia, reaching about 6,961 metres. It is the tallest peak in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres and a major mountaineering objective.

title: Ural Mountains
text: The Ural Mountains run north to south through western Russia and are traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia. Rich in minerals, they are a modest but historically and geographically significant range.

title: Atlas Mountains
text: The Atlas Mountains stretch across northwestern Africa through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia. They separate the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts from the Sahara Desert and are home to Berber communities and snow-capped peaks.

title: Appalachian Mountains
text: The Appalachian Mountains run along the eastern United States and into Canada. Ancient and heavily eroded, they are lower and more rounded than younger ranges and are cloaked in extensive forests.

title: Mount Denali
text: Denali, formerly known as Mount McKinley, in Alaska is the highest mountain peak in North America. Rising over 6,000 metres, it dominates the surrounding wilderness and is known for extreme cold and challenging climbing conditions.

title: Sahara Desert
text: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa. A vast expanse of sand seas, rocky plateaus, and gravel plains, it experiences extreme heat and very little rainfall across an area comparable to a continent.

title: Arabian Desert
text: The Arabian Desert covers much of the Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia. It includes the Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, one of the largest continuous sand deserts in the world, with towering dunes and scorching temperatures.

title: Gobi Desert
text: The Gobi Desert stretches across northern China and southern Mongolia. A cold desert with harsh temperature extremes, it consists largely of bare rock and gravel and is known for fossil discoveries, including dinosaur eggs.

title: Kalahari Desert
text: The Kalahari is a large semi-arid savanna covering parts of Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa. Despite its dryness, it supports grasses and wildlife, and is home to the Indigenous San people.

title: Atacama Desert
text: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth, with some areas having recorded no rainfall for years. Its clear skies and high altitude make it a prime location for astronomical observatories.

title: Antarctic Desert
text: Antarctica is technically the largest desert in the world, classified by its extremely low precipitation. Beneath its thick ice sheet lies a frozen continent, making it a cold, polar desert rather than a hot, sandy one.

title: Mojave Desert
text: The Mojave Desert lies in the southwestern United States, largely in California and Nevada. Known for the distinctive Joshua trees and hot summer temperatures, it contains Death Valley, one of the hottest places on Earth.

title: Namib Desert
text: The Namib Desert stretches along the Atlantic coast of Namibia and is considered one of the oldest deserts in the world. It is famous for its towering red sand dunes, some among the tallest on Earth, meeting the sea along the Skeleton Coast.

title: Thar Desert
text: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, spans northwestern India and eastern Pakistan. It is a densely populated desert region known for its shifting sand dunes and colorful cultural traditions.

title: Lake Baikal
text: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest and one of the oldest freshwater lakes in the world. It holds a large share of the planet's unfrozen fresh water and hosts unique species found nowhere else, including the freshwater Baikal seal.

title: Caspian Sea
text: The Caspian Sea, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan, is the largest inland body of water on Earth. Though called a sea, it is landlocked and contains slightly salty water.

title: Lake Superior
text: Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes of North America and the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area. Shared by the United States and Canada, it is known for its cold, clear waters and rugged shorelines.

title: Lake Victoria
text: Lake Victoria in East Africa is the largest lake in Africa by area, bordered by Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya. A source of the Nile River, it supports millions of people through fishing and transport.

title: Great Lakes
text: The Great Lakes of North America, Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario, form the largest group of freshwater lakes on Earth by total area. Straddling the border of the United States and Canada, they are vital for shipping and water supply.

title: Dead Sea
text: The Dead Sea, bordered by Jordan and Israel, is a salt lake whose surface is the lowest point on Earth's land surface. Its extremely high salinity makes swimmers float easily and prevents most life from surviving in its waters.

title: Lake Tanganyika
text: Lake Tanganyika in East Africa is the second-deepest lake in the world and one of the longest. Bordered by four countries, it holds a vast volume of fresh water and hosts many unique fish species.

title: Lake Titicaca
text: Lake Titicaca, on the border of Peru and Bolivia high in the Andes, is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world. It holds cultural significance for Andean peoples and is dotted with inhabited islands, some of them floating reed platforms.

title: Angel Falls
text: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, plunging over 900 metres from a flat-topped mountain called a tepui. Located in a remote rainforest, it is a spectacular natural wonder of South America.

title: Iguazu Falls
text: Iguazu Falls, on the border of Argentina and Brazil, is a vast system of hundreds of cascades along the Iguazu River. Surrounded by lush rainforest, its most dramatic section is the horseshoe-shaped Devil's Throat.

title: Greenland
text: Greenland is the world's largest island, located between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans. An autonomous territory of Denmark, most of it is covered by a thick ice sheet, and its population is concentrated along the ice-free coast.

title: Borneo
