text: Borneo is the third-largest island in the world, shared by Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei in Southeast Asia. Covered in tropical rainforest, it is home to unique wildlife such as orangutans and the elusive proboscis monkey.

title: Madagascar island
text: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world, lying in the Indian Ocean off southeastern Africa. Long isolated, it evolved a remarkable array of plants and animals found nowhere else, including lemurs and baobab trees.

title: Great Britain island
text: Great Britain is the largest island in Europe, comprising England, Scotland, and Wales. Separated from mainland Europe by the English Channel and North Sea, it has a long maritime history and varied landscapes.

title: Honshu
text: Honshu is the largest and most populous island of Japan, home to major cities including Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto. It contains Mount Fuji and forms the cultural and economic heart of the country.

title: Galapagos Islands
text: The Galapagos Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean belonging to Ecuador. Their isolated ecosystems inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution, and they host unique species such as giant tortoises and marine iguanas.

title: Hawaiian Islands
text: The Hawaiian Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the central Pacific Ocean forming the U.S. state of Hawaii. Known for beaches, active volcanoes, and lush landscapes, they are among the most remote island groups in the world.

title: Iceland island
text: Iceland is a volcanic island in the North Atlantic that sits atop the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two tectonic plates pull apart. Its dramatic landscape features glaciers, geysers, volcanoes, and geothermal springs.

title: Sicily
text: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, lying off the southern tip of Italy of which it is a part. It is home to Mount Etna, one of the world's most active volcanoes, and a rich blend of ancient cultures.

title: Cuba island
text: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, lying south of Florida. Long and narrow, it features fertile plains, mountains, and beaches, and its climate and soil support tobacco and sugar cultivation.

title: Tasmania
text: Tasmania is an island state of Australia lying south of the mainland across the Bass Strait. Known for its rugged wilderness, national parks, and unique wildlife such as the Tasmanian devil, much of it remains pristine.

title: New Guinea island
text: New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world, divided between Papua New Guinea and Indonesia. Covered in dense rainforest and rugged mountains, it is one of the most biologically and culturally diverse places on Earth.

title: Niger River
text: The Niger is the principal river of West Africa, following a great arc through several countries before reaching the Atlantic in Nigeria. Its inland delta in Mali supports fishing and farming in an otherwise dry region.

title: Murray River
text: The Murray is the longest river in Australia, flowing from the eastern highlands across the continent's southeast to the Southern Ocean. Together with the Darling, it forms a river system vital for the country's agriculture.

title: Tigris and Euphrates
text: The Tigris and Euphrates are two great rivers of Western Asia that flow through Iraq. The land between them, known as Mesopotamia, is often called the cradle of civilization, where some of the earliest cities arose.

title: Rio Grande
text: The Rio Grande is a major river of North America that forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico. Flowing from the Rocky Mountains to the Gulf of Mexico, it is a vital water source for arid regions.

title: Orinoco River
text: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers in South America, flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic Ocean. Its vast basin includes wetlands and forests, and it is home to distinctive wildlife such as the Orinoco crocodile.

title: Parana River
text: The Parana is a major river of South America, flowing through Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. Second in length on the continent only to the Amazon, it is an important route for shipping and hydroelectric power.

title: Elbe River
text: The Elbe is a major river of Central Europe, rising in the Czech mountains and flowing through Germany to the North Sea. The port of Hamburg lies along its lower course, making it an important trade artery.

title: Po River
text: The Po is the longest river in Italy, flowing eastward across the fertile northern plains to the Adriatic Sea. Its broad valley is Italy's agricultural and industrial heartland.

title: Loire River
text: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing through the country to the Atlantic Ocean. Its valley is renowned for magnificent Renaissance chateaux and vineyards and is a UNESCO World Heritage region.

title: Brahmaputra River
text: The Brahmaputra is a major river of Asia, flowing from Tibet through India and Bangladesh, where it joins the Ganges. Its enormous delta is one of the most fertile and densely populated regions in the world.

title: Amur River
text: The Amur is a major river of Northeast Asia, forming much of the border between Russia and China. It flows into the Pacific Ocean and is known for its rich fisheries and forested surroundings.

title: Lena River
text: The Lena is one of the great rivers of Siberia in Russia, flowing north to the Arctic Ocean. Frozen for much of the year, it drains a vast, sparsely populated wilderness and forms a large delta.

title: Colorado desert river
text: The Snake River flows through the northwestern United States, cutting deep canyons across the Columbia Plateau before joining the Columbia River. It is important for irrigation and hydroelectric power in the region.

title: Mount Kosciuszko
text: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain on the Australian mainland, in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales. Relatively gentle compared with the world's great peaks, its summit can be reached by walking trails.

title: Carpathian Mountains
text: The Carpathians are a mountain range that arcs through Central and Eastern Europe, including Romania, Slovakia, and Poland. Cloaked in forest, they harbor Europe's largest populations of bears, wolves, and lynx.

title: Pyrenees
text: The Pyrenees form a mountain range separating France from Spain along their shared border, with the tiny state of Andorra nestled among the peaks. They stretch between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Caucasus Mountains
text: The Caucasus Mountains stretch between the Black and Caspian Seas, often regarded as a boundary between Europe and Asia. They contain Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe, and a great diversity of languages and cultures.

title: Mount Elbrus
text: Mount Elbrus, in the Caucasus of southern Russia, is the highest mountain in Europe, a dormant volcano with twin snow-capped summits. It is a popular objective for mountaineers seeking to climb Europe's highest point.

title: Tian Shan
text: The Tian Shan, meaning Celestial Mountains, is a vast range in Central Asia stretching across several countries. Its snow-capped peaks and glaciers feed rivers vital to the arid lands below.

title: Great Dividing Range
text: The Great Dividing Range runs along the eastern edge of Australia, separating the coastal plains from the interior. Although not very high, it is one of the longest mountain ranges in the world and shapes the continent's rivers.

title: Drakensberg
text: The Drakensberg is the highest mountain range in Southern Africa, forming a dramatic escarpment mainly in South Africa and Lesotho. Known for its basalt cliffs and ancient rock art, it is a scenic wilderness area.

title: Sierra Nevada USA
text: The Sierra Nevada is a mountain range in the western United States, mostly in California. It contains giant sequoia groves, the deep valley of Yosemite, and the highest peak in the contiguous states, Mount Whitney.

title: Mount Vesuvius
text: Mount Vesuvius is an active volcano near Naples, Italy, famous for its eruption in AD 79 that buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum. It remains one of the most closely watched volcanoes in the world.

title: Mount Etna
text: Mount Etna on the island of Sicily is one of the most active volcanoes in the world and the highest in Europe outside the Caucasus. Its frequent eruptions have shaped the surrounding landscape and enriched the soil.

title: Mauna Loa
text: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is one of the largest volcanoes on Earth by volume, a broad shield volcano that has built up much of the Big Island. It remains active and rises gently from the surrounding Pacific Ocean floor.

title: Table Mountain
text: Table Mountain is a flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town, South Africa. Its distinctive level summit, often draped in a cloud called the tablecloth, is a national symbol and a popular destination reached by cable car.

title: Patagonia
text: Patagonia is a sparsely populated region at the southern end of South America, shared by Argentina and Chile. Known for windswept steppes, glaciers, and jagged Andean peaks, it is one of the world's great wilderness areas.

title: The Outback
text: The Outback is the vast, remote interior of Australia, characterized by arid deserts, red earth, and scattered settlements. It holds iconic landmarks such as Uluru and is central to Aboriginal culture and Australian identity.

title: The Sahel
text: The Sahel is a broad semi-arid belt across Africa that lies between the Sahara Desert to the north and wetter savannas to the south. It stretches across the continent and is vulnerable to drought and desertification.

title: Amazon Rainforest
text: The Amazon Rainforest in South America is the largest tropical rainforest in the world, spread mainly across Brazil. Home to an immense diversity of plants and animals, it plays a major role in the global climate and carbon cycle.

title: Congo Rainforest
text: The Congo Rainforest in Central Africa is the second-largest tropical rainforest in the world. Spanning several countries around the Congo River basin, it shelters forest elephants, gorillas, and countless other species.

title: Serengeti
text: The Serengeti is a vast plain in East Africa, mostly in Tanzania, famed for its wildlife. It hosts the great migration, in which millions of wildebeest and zebra move across the grasslands in search of fresh grazing.

title: Pampas
text: The Pampas are fertile lowland plains in southern South America, mainly in Argentina and Uruguay. These grasslands are the heartland of cattle ranching and the culture of the gaucho, the South American cowboy.

title: Steppe of Central Asia
text: The steppe is a vast belt of grassland stretching across Central Asia and Eastern Europe. Historically home to nomadic horse-riding peoples, it forms one of the largest continuous grassland regions on the planet.

title: Lake Geneva
text: Lake Geneva is a large lake shared by Switzerland and France, set at the foot of the Alps. Its shores are lined with vineyards, resorts, and cities such as Geneva and Lausanne, and it is fed and drained by the Rhone River.

title: Lake Malawi
text: Lake Malawi is a large lake in East Africa bordered by Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania. Famed for its exceptional variety of colorful fish, especially cichlids, it is one of the deepest lakes on the continent.

title: Great Salt Lake
text: The Great Salt Lake in Utah, USA, is a large saltwater lake, the remnant of a much larger prehistoric lake. Its high salinity supports brine shrimp and attracts vast numbers of migratory birds.

title: Loch Ness
text: Loch Ness is a large, deep freshwater lake in the Scottish Highlands. Famous around the world for legends of a mysterious monster said to inhabit its dark waters, it holds a great volume of water in a long, narrow basin.

title: Aral Sea
text: The Aral Sea in Central Asia was once one of the largest lakes in the world but has shrunk dramatically after rivers feeding it were diverted for irrigation. Its decline is a well-known example of human impact on the environment.

title: Fjords of Norway
text: Fjords are long, deep, narrow inlets of the sea flanked by steep cliffs, formed by glaciers. Norway's coastline is famous for its fjords, such as the Sognefjord, which cut far inland and create dramatic scenery.

title: Canary Islands
text: The Canary Islands are a Spanish archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean off the northwest coast of Africa. Volcanic in origin, they enjoy a mild climate year-round and are a popular destination for beach and nature tourism.

title: Azores
text: The Azores are a Portuguese archipelago of volcanic islands in the North Atlantic Ocean. Known for green landscapes, crater lakes, and hot springs, they lie far out in the ocean between Europe and North America.

title: Maldives atolls
text: The Maldives consists of a chain of coral atolls in the Indian Ocean. Rings of coral surrounding shallow lagoons, these atolls form some of the lowest-lying land on Earth and support renowned marine ecosystems.

title: Faroe Islands
text: The Faroe Islands are a rugged, remote archipelago in the North Atlantic, an autonomous territory of Denmark. Known for steep green cliffs, sheep, and frequent fog, they lie between Iceland and Norway.

title: Zanzibar archipelago
text: The Zanzibar archipelago lies off the coast of Tanzania in the Indian Ocean. Historically a hub of the spice and ivory trade, its islands blend African, Arab, and Indian influences and are ringed by coral reefs.

title: Balearic Islands
text: The Balearic Islands are a Spanish archipelago in the western Mediterranean, including Mallorca, Menorca, and Ibiza. Known for beaches, nightlife, and coves, they are a popular European holiday destination.

title: Falkland Islands
text: The Falkland Islands are a remote archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean, a British overseas territory. Windswept and treeless, they are home to large colonies of penguins and other seabirds.

title: Svalbard
text: Svalbard is a remote Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean, far north of the mainland. Covered largely in ice, it is home to polar bears and hosts a global seed vault safeguarding the world's crop diversity.

title: Cape Verde islands
text: Cape Verde is a volcanic archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean off West Africa. Dry and mountainous, its ten islands developed a distinctive Creole culture and are known for their music and mild climate.

title: Seychelles islands
text: The Seychelles is an archipelago in the Indian Ocean made up of granite and coral islands. Known for pristine beaches, giant tortoises, and rare birds, its inner islands are among the oldest ocean islands on Earth.

title: Comoros islands
text: The Comoros is a volcanic archipelago in the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and the African mainland. Its islands are known for fragrant crops such as vanilla, cloves, and ylang-ylang used in perfume.

title: Africa continent
text: Africa is the second-largest continent, spanning both sides of the equator. It is home to the Sahara Desert, the Nile River, the Congo rainforest, and abundant wildlife, and it contains a great diversity of peoples, languages, and cultures.

title: Asia continent
text: Asia is the largest and most populous continent, stretching from the Mediterranean to the Pacific. It contains the highest mountains on Earth in the Himalayas, vast deserts and plains, and ancient civilizations along rivers such as the Indus and Yangtze.

title: Europe continent
text: Europe is a continent in the Northern Hemisphere, bordered by the Atlantic Ocean and the Arctic. Though relatively small, it is densely populated and historically influential, with varied landscapes from the Alps to the northern fjords.

title: North America continent
text: North America is a continent in the Northern Hemisphere stretching from the Arctic to the tropics. It contains the Rocky Mountains, the Great Plains, the Great Lakes, and the Mississippi River, and includes Canada, the United States, and Mexico.

title: South America continent
text: South America is a continent in the Southern Hemisphere, home to the Amazon rainforest and river, the Andes mountains, and the Atacama Desert. It stretches from tropical jungles in the north to the cold reaches of Patagonia in the south.

title: Australia continent
text: Australia is the smallest continent, lying entirely in the Southern Hemisphere. Much of its interior is arid outback, while its coasts hold most of the population. It is known for unique wildlife such as kangaroos and koalas.

title: Antarctica continent
text: Antarctica is the southernmost continent, centered on the South Pole and almost entirely covered by a thick ice sheet. The coldest, driest, and windiest continent, it has no permanent human population but hosts scientific research stations.

title: Pacific Ocean
text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering more area than all the land combined. It stretches from the Arctic to the Southern Ocean and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in the sea.

title: Atlantic Ocean
text: The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean, separating the Americas from Europe and Africa. It contains the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a vast underwater mountain range formed where tectonic plates pull apart.

title: Indian Ocean
text: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean, bordered by Africa, Asia, and Australia. Warm across much of its expanse, it is influenced by seasonal monsoon winds that shape weather across surrounding regions.

title: Arctic Ocean
text: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest ocean, centered on the North Pole. Much of its surface is covered by drifting sea ice, and it is surrounded by the northern coasts of North America, Europe, and Asia.

title: Southern Ocean
text: The Southern Ocean surrounds the continent of Antarctica. Defined by a cold circumpolar current that flows around the globe unobstructed, it plays a major role in regulating Earth's climate and ocean circulation.

title: Mediterranean Sea
text: The Mediterranean Sea is a large sea enclosed by Europe, Africa, and Asia, connected to the Atlantic Ocean through the Strait of Gibraltar. A cradle of ancient civilizations, its shores host many historic cultures and warm coastal climates.

title: Caribbean Sea
text: The Caribbean Sea lies in the western Atlantic, bordered by Central and South America and the arc of the Caribbean islands. Known for warm, clear waters and coral reefs, it is a major destination for tourism and cruises.

title: Red Sea
text: The Red Sea is a narrow sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, connected to the Mediterranean by the Suez Canal and to the Indian Ocean by the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. It is known for warm waters and vibrant coral reefs.

title: Black Sea
text: The Black Sea is an inland sea bordered by Eastern Europe and Western Asia, connected to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits. Several countries, including Turkey, Russia, and Ukraine, line its shores.

title: Baltic Sea
text: The Baltic Sea is a shallow, brackish sea in Northern Europe, nearly enclosed by Scandinavia and mainland Europe. Its waters connect to the North Sea through the Danish straits, and it is bordered by many nations.

title: North Sea
text: The North Sea lies between Great Britain and mainland Europe, part of the Atlantic Ocean. A busy shipping and fishing region, it also holds significant offshore oil and natural gas reserves.

title: Arabian Sea
text: The Arabian Sea is a region of the northern Indian Ocean bordered by the Arabian Peninsula, Iran, Pakistan, and India. It has been an important route for maritime trade for thousands of years.

title: Bay of Bengal
text: The Bay of Bengal is a large bay in the northeastern Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka. The world's largest bay, it receives the waters of great rivers such as the Ganges.

title: Gulf of Mexico
text: The Gulf of Mexico is a large ocean basin bordered by the United States, Mexico, and Cuba. Rich in oil and fisheries, it is fed by the Mississippi River and influences weather across the surrounding region.

title: Persian Gulf
text: The Persian Gulf is a shallow arm of the Indian Ocean between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran. Rich in oil and gas, it is a strategically vital waterway bordered by several oil-producing nations.

title: Suez Canal
text: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway in Egypt linking the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. Opened in 1869, it allows ships to travel between Europe and Asia without sailing around Africa, greatly shortening the journey.

title: Strait of Gibraltar
text: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow passage connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean, separating Spain in Europe from Morocco in Africa. It is a key maritime chokepoint at the western edge of the Mediterranean.

title: Bosphorus Strait
text: The Bosphorus is a narrow strait in Turkey that connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and separates the European and Asian parts of Istanbul. It is one of the world's busiest and most strategic waterways.

title: Strait of Hormuz
text: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. A vital passage for oil shipments, it is one of the most strategically important chokepoints in global energy trade.

title: Strait of Malacca
text: The Strait of Malacca is a narrow sea passage between the Malay Peninsula and the island of Sumatra. One of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, it links the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

title: English Channel
text: The English Channel is the body of water separating southern England from northern France. One of the busiest shipping areas in the world, it is crossed beneath the seabed by the Channel Tunnel rail link.

title: Gulf Stream
text: The Gulf Stream is a powerful warm ocean current that flows from the Gulf of Mexico across the North Atlantic. It carries warm water toward Europe, moderating the climate of western Europe compared with regions at similar latitudes.

title: Tropical climate
text: Tropical climates occur near the equator and are characterized by high temperatures year-round and abundant rainfall. They support lush rainforests and diverse life, and lack the strong seasonal temperature swings found in higher latitudes.

title: Arid climate
text: Arid or desert climates receive very little rainfall and often experience large swings between hot days and cold nights. Vegetation is sparse and specially adapted to conserve water, as in cacti and other drought-tolerant plants.

title: Temperate climate
text: Temperate climates lie between the tropics and the polar regions and feature distinct seasons with moderate temperatures. They support forests, grasslands, and much of the world's agriculture, with warm summers and cool winters.

title: Polar climate
text: Polar climates occur near the North and South Poles and are marked by extreme cold and long periods of darkness or daylight. Ice and snow dominate the landscape, and only hardy life adapted to the cold can survive.

title: Mediterranean climate
text: A Mediterranean climate features hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Found around the Mediterranean Sea and in similar regions such as California and parts of Australia, it supports olive groves, vineyards, and shrubland.

title: Rainforest biome
text: Rainforests are dense, wet forests found mainly in tropical regions near the equator. They receive heavy rainfall, maintain warm temperatures, and host an extraordinary diversity of plants and animals, including many species found nowhere else.

title: Savanna biome
text: A savanna is a grassland biome scattered with trees, found in tropical regions with distinct wet and dry seasons. The African savanna is famous for its herds of grazing animals and the predators that follow them.

title: Tundra biome
text: The tundra is a cold, treeless biome found in Arctic regions and high mountains. Its ground is often frozen as permafrost, and it supports low-growing plants, mosses, and lichens along with animals adapted to harsh cold.

title: Desert biome
text: The desert biome is defined by very low precipitation and sparse vegetation. Deserts can be hot, like the Sahara, or cold, like the Gobi, and their plants and animals are specially adapted to survive with little water.

title: Grassland biome
text: Grasslands are biomes dominated by grasses rather than trees, found where rainfall is moderate. They include the prairies of North America, the steppes of Eurasia, and the pampas of South America, and are important for grazing and agriculture.

title: Taiga biome
text: The taiga, or boreal forest, is a vast belt of coniferous forest stretching across the northern parts of North America, Europe, and Asia. It endures long, cold winters and is one of the largest land biomes on Earth.

title: Coral reef biome
text: Coral reefs are underwater ecosystems built by tiny animals called coral polyps in warm, shallow tropical seas. Often called the rainforests of the sea, they support an immense diversity of marine life despite covering a small area of the ocean.

title: The Equator
text: The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, equidistant from the North and South Poles. It divides the planet into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres and marks the region where sunlight is most direct year-round.

title: Prime Meridian
text: The Prime Meridian is the line of zero degrees longitude, running through Greenwich in London. It serves as the reference for measuring longitude east and west and as the basis for the world's standard time zones.

title: Latitude and longitude
text: Latitude and longitude are coordinates used to locate any point on Earth. Latitude measures distance north or south of the equator, while longitude measures distance east or west of the Prime Meridian, together forming a global grid.

title: Northern and Southern Hemispheres
text: The Northern and Southern Hemispheres are the halves of the Earth divided by the equator. Seasons are reversed between them, so when it is summer in one it is winter in the other, and most of the world's land lies in the north.

title: Tropic of Cancer
text: The Tropic of Cancer is a line of latitude marking the northernmost point where the sun can appear directly overhead. It passes through regions including Mexico, North Africa, and southern Asia and defines the northern edge of the tropics.

title: Tropic of Capricorn
text: The Tropic of Capricorn is a line of latitude marking the southernmost point where the sun can appear directly overhead. It crosses South America, southern Africa, and Australia and defines the southern edge of the tropics.

title: Time zones
text: Time zones divide the world into regions that share the same standard time, roughly following lines of longitude. As one travels east or west across them, clocks are set forward or back, usually in increments of one hour.

title: International Date Line
text: The International Date Line is an imaginary line roughly following 180 degrees longitude in the Pacific Ocean. Crossing it changes the calendar date, so travelers moving west gain a day and those moving east lose one.

title: Arctic and Antarctic Circles
text: The Arctic and Antarctic Circles are lines of latitude near the poles beyond which the sun does not set on the summer solstice or rise on the winter solstice, producing the phenomena of the midnight sun and polar night.

title: Continental drift
text: Continental drift is the idea, now explained by plate tectonics, that the continents slowly move across the Earth's surface over millions of years. This movement shapes mountains, oceans, and the arrangement of the landmasses over time.

title: Ring of Fire
text: The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean where many of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur. It marks the boundaries of tectonic plates and includes regions such as Japan, Indonesia, and the Andes.

title: California, USA
text: California is a state on the west coast of the United States, the most populous in the country. Its capital is Sacramento, and it is known for Hollywood, Silicon Valley, redwood forests, and a long Pacific coastline.

title: Texas, USA
text: Texas is a large state in the south-central United States, with Austin as its capital. Known for its ranching, oil industry, and distinctive culture, it borders Mexico and stretches from deserts to the Gulf coast.

title: Florida, USA
text: Florida is a state in the southeastern United States, a low-lying peninsula between the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. Its capital is Tallahassee, and it is known for beaches, the Everglades wetlands, and theme parks near Orlando.

title: New York State, USA
text: New York is a state in the northeastern United States, with Albany as its capital, though New York City is by far its largest city. It ranges from the Atlantic coast to the Adirondack Mountains and shares Niagara Falls with Canada.

title: Alaska, USA
text: Alaska is the largest state in the United States by area, in the far northwest of North America. Its capital is Juneau, and it is known for vast wilderness, glaciers, mountains including Denali, and long polar days and nights.

title: Hawaii, USA
text: Hawaii is a state of the United States made up of a volcanic island chain in the central Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Honolulu, and it is known for beaches, active volcanoes, and a distinctive Polynesian-influenced culture.

title: Nevada, USA
text: Nevada is a state in the western United States, largely covered by desert and mountains. Its capital is Carson City, though Las Vegas is its largest city, famous for casinos and entertainment in the Mojave Desert.

title: Colorado, USA
text: Colorado is a state in the western United States dominated by the Rocky Mountains. Its capital, Denver, is nicknamed the Mile-High City for its elevation, and the state is known for skiing and dramatic mountain scenery.

title: Arizona, USA
text: Arizona is a state in the southwestern United States known for its desert landscapes. Its capital is Phoenix, and it is home to the Grand Canyon, saguaro cacti, and a hot, dry climate across much of its territory.

title: Louisiana, USA
text: Louisiana is a state in the southern United States on the Gulf of Mexico. Its capital is Baton Rouge, but New Orleans is its most famous city, known for jazz, Creole and Cajun culture, and the Mississippi River delta.

title: Ontario, Canada
text: Ontario is the most populous province of Canada, home to the national capital Ottawa and the largest city, Toronto. It borders the Great Lakes and Niagara Falls and is a center of the country's economy and government.

title: Quebec, Canada
text: Quebec is the largest province of Canada by area and the heart of French-speaking Canada. Its capital is Quebec City, and its largest city is Montreal. French is the official language, and it has a distinct cultural identity.

title: British Columbia, Canada
text: British Columbia is a province on the west coast of Canada, bordering the Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Victoria, and its largest city is Vancouver. It is known for mountains, forests, and a mild coastal climate.

title: Scandinavia
text: Scandinavia is a region of Northern Europe traditionally comprising Norway, Sweden, and Denmark, sometimes extended to include Finland and Iceland as the Nordic countries. It is known for fjords, forests, and high living standards.

title: The Balkans
text: The Balkans is a region of Southeastern Europe covering countries on the Balkan Peninsula, such as Serbia, Croatia, Greece, and Bulgaria. Mountainous and ethnically diverse, it has a long and complex history at the crossroads of empires.

title: The Middle East
text: The Middle East is a region spanning Western Asia and parts of North Africa, including countries such as Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Turkey. The birthplace of major world religions, it holds much of the world's oil reserves.

title: Sub-Saharan Africa
text: Sub-Saharan Africa refers to the part of the African continent lying south of the Sahara Desert. It encompasses a vast diversity of peoples, languages, landscapes, and ecosystems, from rainforests to savannas.

title: Southeast Asia
text: Southeast Asia is a region between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, including countries such as Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, and the Philippines. Known for tropical climates, rice cultivation, and cultural diversity, it lies along major trade routes.

title: Central America
text: Central America is the narrow land bridge connecting North and South America, including countries such as Guatemala, Costa Rica, and Panama. It features volcanoes, rainforests, and coasts on both the Pacific and Caribbean.

title: The Caribbean
text: The Caribbean is a region of islands in the Caribbean Sea, including nations such as Cuba, Jamaica, and the Bahamas. Known for beaches, warm climate, and diverse cultures blending African, European, and Indigenous influences.

title: The Mediterranean region
text: The Mediterranean region surrounds the Mediterranean Sea, spanning parts of southern Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia. It shares a mild climate, olive and grape cultivation, and a deep history of ancient civilizations.

title: The Arctic
text: The Arctic is the northernmost region of Earth, centered on the North Pole and the Arctic Ocean. Covered by sea ice and tundra, it is home to Indigenous peoples and wildlife such as polar bears, walruses, and reindeer.

title: Polynesia
text: Polynesia is a vast region of the central and southern Pacific Ocean encompassing many island groups, including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, and New Zealand. Its peoples share related languages and a remarkable seafaring heritage.

title: Melanesia
text: Melanesia is a region of the southwestern Pacific Ocean that includes Papua New Guinea, Fiji, the Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu. It is one of the most culturally and linguistically diverse regions in the world.

title: The Iberian Peninsula
text: The Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe is occupied mainly by Spain and Portugal, along with tiny Andorra and Gibraltar. Bordered by the Atlantic and Mediterranean, it has a rich blend of Roman, Moorish, and Christian heritage.

title: The Horn of Africa
text: The Horn of Africa is a peninsula in Northeast Africa jutting into the Arabian Sea, including Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti. Strategically located near key shipping routes, it has ancient cultures and varied landscapes.

title: The Levant
text: The Levant is a region of the eastern Mediterranean in Western Asia, including areas of Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, and neighboring lands. A historic crossroads of trade and religion, it holds many ancient cities and sacred sites.

title: The Great Plains
text: The Great Plains is a vast expanse of flat grassland in central North America, stretching across parts of Canada and the United States. Historically home to bison herds and Indigenous peoples, it is now a major agricultural region.

title: Siberia
text: Siberia is a vast region of northern Asia making up much of Russia. Known for its harsh, cold climate, immense forests, and sparse population, it holds great mineral wealth and the deep waters of Lake Baikal.

title: The Silk Road
text: The Silk Road was a network of ancient trade routes connecting East Asia with the Mediterranean. It carried silk, spices, and ideas across Central Asia, linking civilizations and giving rise to fabled cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara.

title: Mandarin Chinese language
text: Mandarin Chinese is the most widely spoken language in the world by number of native speakers. The official language of China and Taiwan, it is written with Chinese characters and uses tones to distinguish meaning.

title: English language
text: English is a West Germanic language that has become the most widely used language for international communication. Official or dominant in many countries, it serves as a common second language in business, science, and travel worldwide.

title: Spanish language
text: Spanish is a Romance language and the official language of Spain and most of Latin America. One of the most spoken languages in the world, it descends from Latin and is widely used across the Americas.

title: Hindi language
text: Hindi is an Indo-Aryan language and one of the official languages of India, widely spoken across the northern part of the country. It is written in the Devanagari script and has hundreds of millions of speakers.

title: Arabic language
text: Arabic is a Semitic language spoken across the Middle East and North Africa and used in Islamic worship worldwide. Written from right to left, it has many regional dialects united by a shared classical form.

title: French language
text: French is a Romance language spoken in France and many countries across Africa, Canada, and beyond. Long a language of diplomacy and culture, it remains an official language of numerous international organizations.

title: Portuguese language
text: Portuguese is a Romance language and the official language of Portugal and Brazil, as well as several African nations. Brazil has by far the largest number of Portuguese speakers in the world.

title: Russian language
text: Russian is a Slavic language written in the Cyrillic alphabet and the official language of Russia. Widely spoken across the former Soviet region, it is one of the working languages of the United Nations.

title: Bengali language
text: Bengali is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal. With a rich literary tradition, it has a very large number of native speakers and its own distinctive script.

title: Japanese language
text: Japanese is the language of Japan, written with a combination of Chinese-derived characters and two syllabic scripts. It has no close linguistic relatives and features distinct levels of politeness in speech.

title: Swahili language
text: Swahili is a Bantu language widely used as a common tongue across East Africa. An official language in several countries, it blends African roots with Arabic influences and facilitates communication among diverse peoples.

title: German language
text: German is a West Germanic language spoken in Germany, Austria, and parts of Switzerland. One of the major languages of Europe, it has a long literary and scientific tradition and is known for its compound words.

title: Christianity overview
text: Christianity is the world's largest religion, based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth. Practiced across the globe, it includes many branches such as Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant, and its sacred text is the Bible.

title: Islam overview
text: Islam is one of the world's largest religions, founded on the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. Its followers, called Muslims, worship one God, follow the Quran, and undertake practices such as prayer and pilgrimage to Mecca.

title: Hinduism overview
text: Hinduism is one of the oldest major religions, practiced mainly in India and Nepal. It encompasses a wide range of beliefs and traditions, including the concepts of karma and reincarnation, and reveres many deities.

title: Buddhism overview
text: Buddhism is a major religion and philosophy founded on the teachings of the Buddha in ancient India. It emphasizes overcoming suffering through ethical living, meditation, and wisdom, and is widespread across Asia.

title: Judaism overview
text: Judaism is one of the oldest monotheistic religions, centered on a covenant between God and the Jewish people. Its sacred texts include the Torah, and its traditions have profoundly influenced Western religious thought.

title: Sikhism overview
text: Sikhism is a religion that originated in the Punjab region of South Asia in the 15th century. Founded by Guru Nanak, it teaches devotion to one God, equality of all people, and honest living, and centers on the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

title: Shinto overview
text: Shinto is the Indigenous religion of Japan, centered on the worship of kami, or spirits associated with nature and ancestors. It is expressed through shrines, rituals, and festivals and coexists with Buddhism in Japanese life.

title: Major world religions
text: The major world religions include Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, and Sikhism. Together they shape the beliefs, festivals, and daily practices of billions of people and have deeply influenced art, law, and culture.

title: Passports explained
text: A passport is an official document issued by a national government that identifies a traveler and allows international travel. It is required to enter most foreign countries, and travelers should ensure it remains valid, often for several months beyond a trip.

title: Visas explained
text: A visa is an official permission, often a stamp or document, that allows a traveler to enter, stay in, or pass through a country for a specific purpose and period. Requirements vary widely by nationality and destination, so travelers should check in advance.

title: Jet lag
text: Jet lag is a temporary sleep disruption that occurs when traveling quickly across several time zones, as the body's internal clock adjusts to a new schedule. Staying hydrated, adjusting sleep times, and getting daylight can help ease its effects.

title: Packing for travel
text: Packing well means bringing versatile clothing suited to the destination's climate, along with essential documents, medications, and adapters. Travelers are often advised to pack light, roll clothes to save space, and keep valuables in carry-on luggage.

title: Currency and money abroad
text: When traveling abroad, it helps to carry some local currency and a payment card accepted internationally. Exchange rates and fees vary, and it is wise to notify your bank of travel plans and keep some cash for places that do not accept cards.

title: Tipping customs vary
text: Tipping customs differ greatly around the world. In some countries a service charge is included and tipping is minimal, while in others generous tips are expected. Travelers should learn local norms to avoid giving offense or overpaying.

title: Staying safe while traveling
text: Staying safe abroad involves being aware of your surroundings, safeguarding documents and money, and researching local conditions before you go. Keeping copies of important papers and knowing emergency contacts can help in unexpected situations.

title: Local customs and courtesy
text: Respecting local customs, such as dress codes at religious sites, appropriate greetings, and dining etiquette, shows courtesy and helps travelers connect with people. Learning a few words of the local language is often warmly received.

title: Reading a map
text: A map represents geographic features using symbols, scale, and a compass direction, usually with north at the top. Understanding the legend, scale, and grid lines helps a traveler judge distances and find their way in unfamiliar places.

title: Rail travel
text: Rail travel offers an efficient and scenic way to move between and within countries, especially where networks are extensive. Trains often connect city centers directly, and high-speed lines in some regions rival air travel for shorter distances.

title: Air travel
text: Air travel is the fastest way to cross long distances and connect distant countries. Airports handle check-in, security, and customs, and travelers should allow time for these steps and keep passports and boarding passes accessible.

title: Sea travel
text: Sea travel includes ferries that link coasts and islands as well as cruise ships that visit multiple ports. Once the primary means of crossing oceans, sea voyages remain popular for leisure and for reaching places not served by roads.

title: Understanding jetways and transit
text: Transiting through an airport or station may involve connecting flights or trains, sometimes requiring travelers to pass through security or immigration again. Checking transit visa rules and allowing enough connection time helps avoid missed departures.

title: Compass directions
text: A compass shows direction based on the Earth's magnetic field, pointing toward magnetic north. The four cardinal directions are north, south, east, and west, and understanding them is fundamental to navigation and reading maps.

title: Cultural etiquette abroad
text: Cultural etiquette varies by country and can include rules about removing shoes indoors, using the right hand for eating or greeting, and appropriate gestures. Observing how locals behave and asking politely helps travelers act respectfully.

title: Altitude and travel
text: Traveling to high-altitude destinations such as mountain cities can cause altitude sickness, with symptoms like headache and shortness of breath. Ascending gradually, resting, and staying hydrated help the body adjust to thinner air.

title: Travel health precautions
text: Travelers to certain regions may need vaccinations or preventive medicine against diseases not common at home. Consulting a health professional before departure and practicing safe food and water habits reduce the risk of illness abroad.

title: Weather and seasons when traveling
text: Because seasons are reversed between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, and climates vary widely, travelers should research the weather at their destination for the time of year to pack appropriately and plan activities.

title: Electrical plugs abroad
text: Electrical outlets, plug shapes, and voltages differ between countries. Travelers often need a plug adapter to fit foreign sockets and sometimes a voltage converter, so it helps to check the standards of the destination before packing devices.

title: Travel insurance
text: Travel insurance can cover unexpected events such as medical emergencies, trip cancellations, or lost luggage while abroad. Policies vary widely, and travelers are advised to read the terms carefully and match coverage to their plans.

title: Customs and immigration
text: On arriving in a foreign country, travelers usually pass through immigration, which checks passports and visas, and customs, which regulates goods brought across the border. Declaring items honestly helps avoid fines or delays.

title: Duty-free shopping
text: Duty-free shops at international airports and borders sell certain goods without local taxes or duties to travelers leaving or entering a country. Limits apply to how much can be brought in duty-free, and these vary by destination.

title: Currency exchange rates
text: An exchange rate is the value of one currency compared with another, and it changes over time. Travelers exchanging money should be aware that rates and fees differ between banks, exchange offices, and card providers.

title: Learning local phrases
text: Learning a few basic phrases in the local language, such as greetings, please, thank you, and numbers, can greatly ease travel. Locals often appreciate the effort, and simple courtesy words help smooth everyday interactions abroad.

title: Public transport abroad
text: Many cities offer buses, trams, subways, and trains that provide affordable ways to get around. Travelers benefit from learning the local ticketing system, route maps, and any travel passes available for visitors.

title: Haggling and markets
text: In many parts of the world, bargaining over prices in markets is a normal and expected part of shopping. Where haggling is customary, doing so politely and with good humor is part of the local culture, while fixed-price shops do not negotiate.

title: Respecting sacred sites
text: When visiting temples, mosques, churches, or other sacred places, travelers should dress modestly, remove shoes where required, and behave quietly. Following posted rules and local guidance shows respect for the beliefs of others.

title: Photography etiquette
text: Travelers should be mindful when taking photographs abroad, as some sites, ceremonies, or individuals may not welcome cameras. Asking permission before photographing people and observing signs at religious or sensitive sites is courteous.

title: Time zone differences
text: When traveling across time zones, the local time at the destination may differ by several hours from home. Adjusting watches and phones on arrival and planning calls or connections around the difference helps avoid confusion.

title: Staying hydrated when flying
text: Cabin air on long flights is very dry, which can leave travelers dehydrated. Drinking water regularly, limiting alcohol and caffeine, and moving around the cabin can help travelers feel better during and after a flight.

title: Safe food and water
text: In some regions, tap water may not be safe for visitors to drink, and it is wise to use bottled or treated water, including for brushing teeth. Eating freshly cooked food and peeling fruit are common precautions against illness.

title: Keeping documents safe
text: Travelers are advised to keep passports, tickets, and money secure, often using a hotel safe or a hidden pouch. Carrying copies of important documents separately can help if the originals are lost or stolen abroad.

title: Choosing accommodation
text: Travelers can choose from many types of lodging, including hotels, guesthouses, hostels, and rented apartments. Location, budget, and the kind of experience desired all influence the best choice for a particular trip.

title: Border crossings by land
text: Crossing borders by land, on foot, by car, or by train, may involve passport checks and customs inspections at the frontier. Requirements and waiting times vary, and travelers should carry the correct documents for both countries.

title: Understanding local currency
text: Before spending abroad, it helps to become familiar with the local currency's denominations, coins, and rough value in one's home money. This reduces the chance of confusion or overpaying when handling unfamiliar notes and coins.

title: Seasons and packing
text: Because climate and season vary by destination, packing should suit local conditions, whether that means light clothing for the tropics or warm layers for cold regions. Checking a forecast before departure helps travelers pack wisely.

title: Navigating with landmarks
text: When maps or signs are unclear, travelers can navigate using prominent landmarks such as towers, rivers, or hills. Noting the position of the sun and memorable features helps orient a person in an unfamiliar place.

title: Scale on a map
text: The scale of a map shows the relationship between distances on the map and real distances on the ground. Understanding scale lets a traveler estimate how far apart places are and how long a journey might take.

title: Contour lines on maps
text: Contour lines on a map connect points of equal elevation, showing the shape of the land. Lines close together indicate steep slopes, while lines spread apart indicate gentle terrain, helping hikers and travelers read the landscape.

title: Compass rose and bearings
text: A compass rose on a map indicates the cardinal directions, and a bearing gives a precise direction measured in degrees. Together they help travelers plan and follow a route accurately across land or water.

title: Global Positioning System
text: The Global Positioning System, or GPS, uses signals from satellites to determine a device's location anywhere on Earth. Widely used in navigation, it lets travelers find their position and directions in real time.

title: Travel and vaccinations
text: Some destinations recommend or require vaccinations against diseases not common at home. Travelers are advised to consult a health provider well before departure, as some vaccines need time to become effective.

title: Motion sickness in travel
text: Motion sickness can affect travelers on boats, planes, cars, or trains when the senses receive conflicting signals about movement. Sitting where motion is felt least, looking at the horizon, and medication can help ease symptoms.

title: Cultural greetings
text: Greetings vary widely around the world, from handshakes and bows to cheek kisses and pressing palms together. Observing how locals greet one another helps travelers respond appropriately and make a good first impression.

title: Dining etiquette abroad
text: Table manners differ between cultures, including how utensils are used, whether to finish everything on the plate, and how to signal appreciation. Watching hosts and following their lead helps travelers dine politely in new settings.

title: Gift-giving customs
text: In many cultures, offering a small gift when visiting someone's home is a gesture of respect. The type of gift, how it is presented, and even the wrapping can carry meaning, so learning local customs helps avoid unintended offense.

title: Dressing appropriately abroad
text: Appropriate dress varies by country and setting, from modest attire at religious sites to formal wear for certain occasions. Respecting local norms of clothing helps travelers show consideration and blend in more comfortably.

title: Understanding jet routes
text: International flights often follow curved paths on a map because the shortest route over the globe is a great circle. This is why a flight between distant cities may pass over regions that seem out of the way on a flat map.

title: Overnight and sleeper trains
text: Sleeper trains allow travelers to journey overnight between distant cities while resting in a berth or cabin. Popular in many parts of Europe and Asia, they combine transport and accommodation in a single trip.

title: Ferries and island travel
text: Ferries connect coastlines and islands, carrying passengers and often vehicles across straits, bays, and channels. In many regions they are an essential and scenic mode of transport where bridges or tunnels are impractical.

title: Reading train timetables
text: Train timetables list departure and arrival times, platforms, and connections. Understanding how to read them, including any symbols for days of operation, helps travelers plan journeys and make connections reliably.

title: Preparing for altitude
text: Travelers heading to high-altitude places should ascend gradually where possible, rest on arrival, and stay hydrated. Because the air holds less oxygen, physical activity may feel harder until the body adjusts over a few days.

title: Coping with heat and sun
text: In hot, sunny climates travelers should protect themselves with sunscreen, hats, and light clothing, drink plenty of water, and avoid strenuous activity during the hottest hours. These steps help prevent sunburn and heat exhaustion.

title: Coping with cold climates
text: In cold regions, dressing in layers traps warm air and allows travelers to adjust to changing conditions. Covering the head and hands, staying dry, and eating well help the body maintain warmth in freezing weather.

title: Local transport etiquette
text: Norms on public transport vary by place, such as queuing, offering seats, keeping quiet, or removing backpacks in crowded carriages. Observing how locals behave helps travelers ride considerately in an unfamiliar city.

title: Souvenirs and export rules
text: Some countries restrict the export of certain items, such as antiquities, protected wildlife products, or plants. Travelers should be aware of these rules to avoid buying souvenirs that cannot legally be taken home.

title: Emergency numbers abroad
text: Different countries use different telephone numbers to reach emergency services such as police, ambulance, or fire. Learning the local emergency number on arrival can be important in case of an urgent situation while traveling.

title: Understanding weather patterns
text: Weather at a destination is shaped by factors such as latitude, altitude, proximity to the sea, and prevailing winds. Understanding these patterns helps travelers anticipate conditions like monsoon rains or dry seasons.

title: Niagara detail
text: Horseshoe Falls is the largest of the three cascades that make up Niagara Falls on the Canada-United States border. Its broad, curving crest carries an enormous volume of water and generates a constant cloud of mist.

title: Gullfoss
text: Gullfoss is a powerful waterfall in southwestern Iceland where a glacial river plunges in two stages into a rugged canyon. Its name means Golden Falls, and it is one of the country's most visited natural sights.

title: Kaieteur Falls
text: Kaieteur Falls in Guyana is one of the world's most powerful single-drop waterfalls, plunging over 200 metres in a single sheet. Surrounded by dense rainforest, it is far larger in volume than many taller falls.

title: Yosemite Falls
text: Yosemite Falls in California is one of the tallest waterfalls in North America, dropping in three sections. Fed by melting snow, it is at its most dramatic in spring and diminishes to a trickle by late summer.

title: Angel Falls detail
text: Angel Falls tumbles from the edge of Auyan-tepui, a flat-topped mountain in Venezuela, so high that much of the water evaporates into mist before reaching the ground. It is named after an aviator who publicized it in the 1930s.

title: Lake Michigan
text: Lake Michigan is one of the five Great Lakes of North America and the only one entirely within the United States. Bordered by several states, it features sandy beaches, dunes, and the major city of Chicago on its shore.

title: Lake Huron
text: Lake Huron is one of the Great Lakes of North America, shared by the United States and Canada. It contains Manitoulin Island, the largest island in a freshwater lake in the world, and thousands of smaller islands.

title: Lake Erie
text: Lake Erie is the shallowest of the Great Lakes of North America, shared by the United States and Canada. Its waters drain over Niagara Falls, and its shores support fishing and agriculture.

title: Lake Ontario
text: Lake Ontario is the easternmost of the Great Lakes, shared by the United States and Canada. It receives water from Niagara Falls and drains into the St. Lawrence River, and the city of Toronto sits on its northern shore.

title: Lake Como
text: Lake Como is a scenic lake in northern Italy at the foot of the Alps, known for its elegant villas and mountainous shores. Long a retreat for the wealthy, it is one of the country's most picturesque destinations.

title: Lake Tahoe
text: Lake Tahoe is a large, deep freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the border of California and Nevada. Famed for its clear blue water and surrounding mountains, it is a popular destination for skiing and summer recreation.

title: Crater Lake
text: Crater Lake in Oregon, USA, is the deepest lake in the United States, formed in the collapsed crater of an ancient volcano. Its intensely blue, exceptionally clear water is fed only by rain and snow.

title: Annapurna
text: Annapurna is a massif in the Himalayas of Nepal that includes several very high peaks. One of the world's tallest mountains, it is renowned among climbers and trekkers, though it has a reputation as especially dangerous to ascend.

title: Kangchenjunga
text: Kangchenjunga, on the border of Nepal and India, is the third-highest mountain in the world. Its name refers to five peaks, and it is regarded as sacred by local communities who traditionally leave its summit untouched.

title: Mount Ararat
text: Mount Ararat is a snow-capped dormant volcano in eastern Turkey, the highest peak in the country. Associated in tradition with the resting place of Noah's Ark, it is a national symbol of neighboring Armenia.

title: Mount Cook
text: Aoraki, or Mount Cook, is the highest mountain in New Zealand, in the Southern Alps of the South Island. Its glaciers and snowfields make it a center for mountaineering and a training ground for famous climbers.

title: Mount Cotopaxi
text: Cotopaxi in Ecuador is one of the highest active volcanoes in the world, rising as a near-perfect snow-capped cone in the Andes. It lies near the equator yet carries a permanent covering of ice and snow.

title: Kilimanjaro glaciers
text: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is unusual for carrying glaciers and snow near its summit despite standing close to the equator. A free-standing volcano, it rises dramatically from surrounding plains as the highest point in Africa.

title: Mount Sinai
text: Mount Sinai is a mountain in the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt, traditionally identified as the place where Moses received the commandments. A site of pilgrimage, it draws visitors who climb to watch the sunrise from its summit.

title: Mount Olympus
text: Mount Olympus is the highest mountain in Greece, celebrated in mythology as the home of the ancient Greek gods. Its cloud-wreathed peaks rise near the Aegean coast and are protected as a national park.

title: Zugspitze
text: The Zugspitze is the highest mountain in Germany, on the border with Austria in the Bavarian Alps. Reached by cog railway and cable car, its summit offers sweeping views across several countries.

title: Yenisei River
text: The Yenisei is one of the great rivers of Siberia in Russia, flowing north to the Arctic Ocean. Draining a vast basin of forest and tundra, it is among the largest river systems in the world by volume.

title: Ob River
text: The Ob is a major river of western Siberia in Russia, flowing north to the Arctic Ocean. Together with its tributary the Irtysh, it forms one of the longest river systems in the world.

title: Darling River
text: The Darling is a major river of eastern Australia, the longest tributary of the Murray. Flowing through dry inland country, it is central to the Murray-Darling system that supports much of the nation's farming.

title: Sao Francisco River
text: The Sao Francisco is a major river of Brazil, flowing through the country's northeast before reaching the Atlantic. Often called the river of national unity, it is a vital water source for a semi-arid region.

title: Dardanelles
text: The Dardanelles is a narrow strait in Turkey connecting the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara, which in turn links to the Black Sea. Together with the Bosphorus, it separates Europe from Asia and is strategically important.

title: Bering Strait
text: The Bering Strait is a narrow passage between Russia and Alaska, connecting the Pacific and Arctic Oceans. It marks the closest point between Asia and North America and lies along the International Date Line.

title: Strait of Dover
text: The Strait of Dover is the narrowest part of the English Channel, separating England from France. One of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, it is where the Channel Tunnel runs beneath the seabed.

title: Cook Strait
text: Cook Strait separates the North and South Islands of New Zealand, connecting the Tasman Sea with the Pacific Ocean. Known for strong currents and winds, it is crossed by ferries linking the two main islands.

title: Gibraltar landmark
text: The Rock of Gibraltar is a towering limestone promontory at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, a British overseas territory. Guarding the strait between the Mediterranean and Atlantic, it is famous for its resident monkeys.

title: Mangrove forests
text: Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees that grow along tropical and subtropical coastlines, their tangled roots rising from the water. They protect shorelines from erosion and storms and provide vital habitat for fish and birds.

title: Wetlands
text: Wetlands are areas where water covers or saturates the soil, including marshes, swamps, and bogs. They filter water, store carbon, control floods, and support rich wildlife, making them among the most productive ecosystems on Earth.

title: Permafrost
text: Permafrost is ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years, found across the Arctic and high mountains. It underlies much of Siberia, Alaska, and northern Canada and stores large amounts of ancient carbon.

title: The Everglades
text: The Everglades in Florida, USA, is a vast subtropical wetland, a slow-moving river of grass. Home to alligators, wading birds, and the rare Florida panther, it is protected as a national park and a unique ecosystem.

title: The Pantanal
text: The Pantanal, mostly in Brazil, is one of the largest tropical wetlands in the world. Flooded for much of the year, it teems with wildlife, including jaguars, caimans, and countless birds, and supports rich biodiversity.

title: Salt flats
text: Salt flats are wide, level expanses of salt left behind when shallow lakes evaporate in dry climates. The Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia and the Bonneville flats in the United States are among the most famous examples.

title: Sand dunes
text: Sand dunes are hills of wind-blown sand found in deserts and along some coasts. Shaped by prevailing winds, they can migrate over time, and some in deserts such as the Namib and Sahara rise hundreds of metres high.

title: Rift valleys
text: A rift valley forms where the Earth's crust is pulled apart, creating a long lowland between highlands. The East African Rift is a prominent example, dotted with lakes and volcanoes as the continent slowly splits.

title: Canyons and gorges
text: A canyon or gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, usually carved by a river over long spans of time. The Grand Canyon in the United States is among the most famous, revealing layers of ancient rock.

title: Caves and caverns
text: Caves are natural underground spaces, often formed as water dissolves rock such as limestone over thousands of years. Some contain spectacular formations of stalactites and stalagmites, and a few host ancient human art.

title: Marrakech vs Rabat note
text: Morocco's largest city is Casablanca, while its capital is Rabat and its most-visited historic city is Marrakech. Each plays a distinct role, illustrating that a country's biggest, best-known, and capital cities can differ.

title: Lagos vs Abuja note
text: Nigeria's political capital is Abuja, a planned city in the country's center, while Lagos on the coast remains the largest city and economic powerhouse. Several countries similarly separate their capital from their biggest city.

title: Sydney vs Canberra note
text: Australia's capital is Canberra, a purpose-built city chosen as a compromise, while Sydney and Melbourne are larger and better known. This reflects a pattern where a planned capital is smaller than the country's leading cities.

title: Washington vs New York note
text: The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C., a planned federal district, while New York City is the largest and most globally famous American city. The seat of government and the largest city are distinct.

title: Ankara vs Istanbul note
text: Turkey's capital is Ankara, chosen for its central location, while Istanbul is far larger and historically prominent, straddling Europe and Asia. The capital and the best-known city of a country are not always the same.

title: Brasilia vs Rio note
text: Brazil's capital is Brasilia, a modernist planned city inaugurated in 1960, which replaced Rio de Janeiro. Rio and Sao Paulo remain larger and more famous, showing how capitals can be deliberately created inland.

title: Ottawa vs Toronto note
text: Canada's capital is Ottawa, chosen partly as a compromise between English and French Canada, while Toronto and Montreal are larger cities. The national capital is smaller than the country's leading urban centers.

title: Bern vs Zurich note
text: Switzerland's capital is Bern, though Zurich and Geneva are larger and internationally better known. Switzerland has no single dominant city, and its federal seat is a moderately sized historic town.

title: Wellington vs Auckland note
text: New Zealand's capital is Wellington, a compact, windy city at the base of the North Island, while Auckland is much larger. The capital and the biggest city differ, a common pattern around the world.

title: Pretoria three capitals note
text: South Africa uniquely has three capitals: Pretoria for the executive, Cape Town for the legislature, and Bloemfontein for the judiciary. This division spreads the branches of government across different cities.

title: Kraków vs Warsaw note
text: Poland's capital is Warsaw, largely rebuilt after wartime destruction, while Krakow preserves an older royal heritage as a former capital. Both are major cities, illustrating how a country's historic and modern capitals can differ.

title: Naples and the south
text: Naples, in southern Italy, is a densely populated port city overlooked by Mount Vesuvius. Regarded as the birthplace of pizza and rich in history, it lies near the ancient ruins of Pompeii and the scenic Amalfi Coast.

title: Genoa, Italy
text: Genoa is a historic port city in northwestern Italy on the Ligurian Sea. Once a powerful maritime republic, it is the birthplace of the explorer Christopher Columbus and features a warren of medieval lanes.

title: Seville and Andalusia
text: Seville, capital of Andalusia in southern Spain, is famed for flamenco, Moorish architecture, and its grand cathedral. The region reflects centuries of Islamic and Christian heritage across cities such as Granada and Cordoba.

title: Granada, Spain
text: Granada is a city in southern Spain at the foot of the Sierra Nevada mountains. It is renowned for the Alhambra, a hilltop palace and fortress that is one of the finest surviving examples of Moorish architecture in the world.

title: Cordoba, Spain
text: Cordoba is a historic city in southern Spain, once a great center of learning under Moorish rule. Its most famous monument is the Mezquita, a vast former mosque with rows of arches, later converted into a cathedral.

title: Toledo, Spain
text: Toledo is a historic hilltop city in central Spain, encircled by a river. Known as the City of Three Cultures for its Christian, Muslim, and Jewish heritage, its medieval old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Strasbourg, France
text: Strasbourg is a city in eastern France near the German border, seat of the European Parliament. Known for its canals, half-timbered houses, and towering cathedral, it blends French and German cultural influences.

title: Bordeaux, France
text: Bordeaux is a city in southwestern France, world-famous as a center of wine production. Set on the Garonne River, it is known for its elegant 18th-century architecture and surrounding vineyards.

title: Vienna coffee culture
text: Vienna, the Austrian capital, is famous for its historic coffee houses, where patrons linger over coffee and pastries. This cafe tradition, along with the city's musical heritage, is central to Viennese culture.

title: Tipping in the United States
text: In the United States, tipping is customary and often expected in restaurants, taxis, and hotels, typically a percentage of the bill. Service workers may rely on tips as a significant part of their income, so visitors should budget for them.

title: Tipping in Japan
text: In Japan, tipping is generally not customary and can even cause confusion or be seen as impolite. Good service is considered standard, and the price charged is usually understood to be complete without an added gratuity.

title: Tipping in Europe
text: Tipping customs vary across Europe. In many countries a service charge may be included in the bill, and rounding up or leaving a small amount is common rather than a large percentage. Norms differ from country to country.

title: Business etiquette abroad
text: Business customs vary worldwide, including how to exchange business cards, appropriate punctuality, and formality of address. Learning local expectations helps travelers make a good impression in professional settings.

title: Personal space and gestures
text: Comfortable personal space and the meaning of gestures differ between cultures. A gesture that is friendly in one country may be rude in another, so travelers benefit from observing local behavior and using gestures cautiously.

title: Bargaining respectfully
text: Where haggling is customary, it is usually expected to be good-natured rather than aggressive. Starting with a friendly attitude, knowing roughly what an item is worth, and being willing to walk away are part of the process.

title: Modest dress at holy sites
text: Many religious sites require modest dress, such as covering shoulders, knees, or the head. Carrying a scarf or extra layer allows travelers to comply respectfully when visiting temples, mosques, churches, or shrines.

title: Removing shoes indoors
text: In many countries, including much of Asia, it is customary to remove shoes before entering homes and some temples. Travelers should watch for shoes left at doorways as a sign of this practice and follow the local custom.

title: Queuing customs
text: Attitudes toward lining up, or queuing, vary between places. In some countries orderly queues are strongly expected, while in others crowding is more common. Observing local norms helps travelers behave courteously.

title: Public behavior norms
text: Norms about noise, eating in public, or displays of affection differ around the world. Being aware that behavior acceptable at home may not be elsewhere helps travelers avoid causing unintended offense.

title: Latitude lines explained
text: Lines of latitude, also called parallels, run east to west around the globe and measure distance north or south of the equator. The equator is zero degrees, and the poles are at ninety degrees north and south.

title: Longitude lines explained
text: Lines of longitude, also called meridians, run from pole to pole and measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. They converge at the poles and are widest apart at the equator.

title: The four cardinal points
text: The four cardinal points are north, south, east, and west. North typically points toward the top of a map and toward the North Pole, and understanding these directions is essential for navigation and orientation.

title: Coordinated Universal Time
text: Coordinated Universal Time, or UTC, is the primary time standard by which the world regulates clocks. Time zones are defined as offsets from UTC, and it is based on the time at the Prime Meridian near Greenwich.

title: Daylight saving time
text: Daylight saving time is the practice of moving clocks forward in spring and back in autumn to make better use of daylight. Not all countries observe it, and the dates vary, which can affect travel and international scheduling.

title: Continents and oceans overview
text: Earth's surface is divided into seven continents, Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia, and Antarctica, and five oceans, the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, and Southern. Together they cover the globe.

title: Land and water proportions
text: About seven-tenths of the Earth's surface is covered by water, most of it in the oceans, while land makes up the remainder. This is why Earth is sometimes called the blue planet when seen from space.

title: Mapping projections
text: A map projection is a way of representing the round Earth on a flat surface, which inevitably distorts some features. Different projections preserve area, shape, or distance to varying degrees, so no flat map is perfectly accurate.

title: The compass and magnetic north
text: A magnetic compass points toward magnetic north, which differs slightly from true north, the direction of the North Pole. Navigators account for this difference, called declination, when plotting accurate courses.

title: Elevation and climate
text: Temperature generally decreases with altitude, so high mountains can be cold even in tropical regions. This is why snow-capped peaks exist near the equator and why mountain climates differ from the lowlands around them.

title: Latitude and climate
text: Climate is strongly influenced by latitude, since regions near the equator receive more direct sunlight and are warmer, while polar regions receive slanting rays and are colder. This helps explain the world's broad climate zones.

title: Prevailing winds
text: Prevailing winds are the dominant directions from which winds blow in a region, such as the trade winds near the equator and the westerlies in temperate zones. They shape weather, ocean currents, and historic sailing routes.

title: Biodiversity hotspots
text: Certain regions, such as tropical rainforests and coral reefs, hold an exceptional variety of plant and animal life. These biodiversity hotspots are especially rich and often especially threatened by human activity.

title: Migration of animals
text: Many animals undertake seasonal migrations across great distances, such as the wildebeest of the Serengeti or migratory birds crossing continents. These journeys are shaped by climate, food, and breeding needs.

title: National parks worldwide
text: National parks are areas protected by governments to conserve natural landscapes and wildlife. Found on every inhabited continent, they preserve places such as Yellowstone, the Serengeti, and Banff for future generations.

title: Endangered species and habitats
text: Many species around the world are endangered due to habitat loss, hunting, and climate change. Conservation efforts, including protected areas and breeding programs, aim to safeguard animals such as tigers, rhinos, and gorillas.

title: Coastlines and beaches
text: Coastlines are the boundaries between land and sea, shaped over time by waves, tides, and currents. They include beaches, cliffs, and estuaries, and are among the most populated and visited environments on Earth.

title: Rivers and civilization
text: Great civilizations often arose along rivers, which provided water, fertile soil, and transport. The Nile, Tigris and Euphrates, Indus, and Yellow rivers each nurtured some of the earliest urban societies in human history.

title: Trade routes in history
text: Historic trade routes such as the Silk Road and maritime spice routes connected distant regions, carrying goods, ideas, and cultures. They shaped the growth of cities and the exchange of knowledge across continents.

title: The importance of ports
text: Port cities, where ships load and unload goods, have long been centers of trade and cultural exchange. Places such as Singapore, Rotterdam, and Shanghai owe much of their importance to their harbors and shipping links.

title: Wellington windy city note
text: Wellington, New Zealand's capital, is nicknamed the Windy City for the strong gusts funneled through the Cook Strait. Compact and hilly, it is known for its arts, cafes, and harbor setting at the base of the North Island.

title: Canberra planned capital note
text: Canberra, the Australian capital, was designed in the early 20th century with a layout of geometric avenues around an artificial lake. As a planned city, it contrasts with the organic growth of Sydney and Melbourne.

title: La Paz altitude note
text: La Paz, the administrative capital of Bolivia, sits in a high Andean basin and is among the highest cities of its size in the world. Its dramatic setting means visitors may need time to adjust to the thin mountain air.

title: Quito equator note
text: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, lies very close to the equator high in the Andes. A monument nearby marks the equatorial line, where visitors can stand with a foot in each hemisphere of the Earth.

title: Singapore garden city note
text: Singapore is often called a garden city for its abundant greenery, vertical gardens, and tree-lined roads integrated into a dense urban environment. It combines a tropical climate with meticulous planning and cleanliness.

title: Dubai desert city note
